title: Pre-trained Invertible Neural Network Assisted High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimization Framework for Wind Farm Layout Design
abstract: Wake effects in wind farms degrade energy capture and turbine reliability, underscoring the importance of layout optimization. Existing studies either rely on analytical wake models at the expense of accuracy or combine numerical wake models with heuristic algorithms at the expense of efficiency. In contrast, we propose a pre-trained invertible neural network assisted high-dimensional Bayesian optimization framework for wind farm layout design, achieving both high accuracy and high efficiency. Specifically, this study employs a high-fidelity numerical wake model to ensure accurate wake estimation and develops a Bayesian optimization (BO)–based framework to enhance search efficiency. An invertible neural network (INN) is specifically designed and, for the first time, integrated with BO to alleviate the curse of dimensionality in high-dimensional layout spaces. The proposed INN-BO framework is evaluated under five distinct and progressively complex scenarios, including the real offshore data from California. Comparative evaluations against state-of-the-art algorithms demonstrate that INN-BO achieves superior solution quality with reduced convergence time, highlighting its strong generalizability and practical relevance to real-world wind farm design.

title: Stability Analysis of Grid-Forming Inverter-Based Resources Using Sequence Immittance Modeling and Dual Feedback Loop Criteria
abstract: Sequence immittance framework is an effective method to analyze the frequency-domain stability between the inverter-based resource (IBR) and the grid. However, there is a lack of a generic sequence immittance stability analysis framework for grid-forming inverter-based resource (GFM-IBR) considering frequency coupling and AC-DC coupling simultaneously. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a stability analysis framework for GFM-IBR using sequence immittance modeling and dual feedback loop criteria. Firstly, GFM-IBR is definitely modeled as impedance with self-stabilization based on two-port network by standardizing the immittance form for frequency coupling and AC-DC coupling. Secondly, the dual feedback loop criteria, integrating frequency coupling and AC-DC coupling, is proposed to avoid the need of checking the right-half-plane (RHP) poles. Finally, cases of grid-connected GFM-IBR verify the correctness of the proposed stability analysis framework. It is revealed that the voltage loop is the main reason for GFM self-stabilization, which makes GFM-IBR to be modeled as the impedance form. Frequency coupling and AC-DC coupling greatly affect the stability of GFM-IBR as short circuit ratio (SCR) increases, which should not be neglected. The nonlinearity in synchronization and control of GFM-IBR affects frequency and AC-DC coupling more than that of grid-following inverter-based resource (GFL-IBR), while both exhibit dual uniformity.

title: Rapid Active Power Regulation of Distributed Photovoltaics Based on Optimal Dynamic Droop Coefficients
abstract: To realize the active response for rapid active power regulation of massive distributed photovoltaics (DPVs), a bi-level architecture integrating clustering and optimization is proposed for the coordinated design of dynamic droop coefficients of DPVs in this paper. At the lower level, the adjustable capacity and response time are selected as clustering features according to the rapid active power regulation requirements, and the U-k-means algorithm is applied to implement the clustering of DPVs. At the upper level, a frequency deviation-optimal droop coefficient model incorporating the regulation performance and network losses is developed in a perspective that considers power flow impacts. The droop coefficient regulation strategy under various frequency fluctuations is pre-calculated by a graph attention network (GAT). Simulations are performed on a modified IEEE 33-bus test system, and the results verify the outperformance of the proposed GAT model over the existing neural network models, as well as the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed optimal droop coefficient regulation strategy.

title: A Looped Operation Optimization Framework for an Electric-Hydrogen Coupled System Using Joint Model-Based and Model-Free Approaches
abstract: Recently, electric–hydrogen coupled systems (EHCS) have gained wide attention. However, the spatiotemporal nonlinear constraints arising from the coupling and interaction of electricity and hydrogen energy flows, together with the persistent disturbances caused by multiple uncertainties from sources, loads, and devices, pose significant challenges to their operational optimization. Accordingly, we propose a dual–loop optimization framework with a joint solving loop (inner loop) and a knowledge correction loop (outer loop). The inner loop employs ADMM to structurally decompose the system optimization into electricity and hydrogen subproblems, mitigating solution–space complexity. It then matches model–based optimization (with its sample–efficiency advantage) to the electricity chain’s quasi–static behavior at the decision timescale, and model–free learning (with its long–horizon decision robustness advantage) to the hydrogen chain’s dynamics and uncertainties, enabling efficient coordinated solving across both chains. The outer loop derives implicit rewards from operational features and expert knowledge to dynamically correct the explicit cost–based reward, providing prior guidance that improves the agent’s learning efficiency. The two loops operate in coordination, forming a customized dual–loop optimization paradigm tailored for coordinated operation of the electricity and hydrogen chains, with the goal of balancing theoretical optimality and practical execution robustness. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Day-Ahead Wind Power Ramp Events Prediction with Extreme-Value–Driven Learning and Confidence-Aware Detection
abstract: Wind power ramp events (WPREs)—sudden, large-magnitude changes in wind generation—pose significant threats to power system stability. Accurate day-ahead prediction of WPREs is critical for proactive scheduling, reserve allocation, and grid security. However, existing methods often struggle with three key limitations: they underperform on rare and extreme events, lack sensitivity to multi-scale temporal dynamics, and provide little to no uncertainty quantification. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel day-ahead WPREs prediction method that integrates three innovations. First, we design an Extreme-Value-Driven Learning model that decomposes wind power into multiple temporal frequency bands, enabling the simultaneous capture of long-term trends and short-term changes. Second, we introduce a tailored extreme-based loss function that rebalances model learning from average-case accuracy toward greater sensitivity to ramp events. Third, we develop a wind power–oriented conformal inference method that produces model-adaptive confidence intervals with formal statistical guarantees, enabling a confidence-aware ramp detection algorithm. Unlike conventional approaches that prioritize mean error metrics, our method is tailored to the operational significance of ramp events. Remarkably, experimental results on two real-world wind power datasets show that our method improves WPREs prediction accuracy by up to 29.6% in terms of F1-score with negligible added computational cost.

title: A Tensor-Based Clustering Method for Dynamic Equivalent Modeling of Wind Farms
abstract: Simulating large-scale wind farms (WFs) with detailed wind turbine (WT) models is computationally costly, which motivates exploration for simplified modeling strategies while maintaining accuracy. However, due to complicated wind speed conditions and network structure, it is still a challenge to achieve accurate transient equivalence of WFs. To address this problem, this paper proposed, for the first time, a tensor decomposition-based clustering method that can capture high-dimensional transient characteristics of WF to achieve precise reduced-order modeling through more rational grouping. More specifically, we first formulate a tensor-structure-based data set to preserve the intrinsic spatio-temporal properties of the dynamic WF responses. Then, a tensor decomposition strategy considering sparsity and smoothness is also proposed to extract the low-dimensional features that further assist us in the clustering design. Finally, we tailor an accurate WF network aggregation strategy to reduce power loss errors. The simulation results for different WF layouts, system faults, and wind scenarios reveal the excellent performance of the proposed method.

title: PMU-Based Power Oscillation Damping Control for Renewable Energy System With Communication Disruption and Multi-Time Delays
abstract: This paper presents a novel model-free power oscillation damping strategy for renewable energy (RE) system considering communication disruption and multiple time delays in control loops. First, a multivariate Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) process-enabled online estimation method is developed for state-space modeling estimation only using measurement data. This estimation method is applicable to systems with different delays in each wide-area control loop. Subsequently, a novel wide-area power oscillation damper (POD) is designed for the renewable energy sources (RESs) and that is further reconstructed in a decomposition manner to achieve independently sub-control, which allows to retain better damping performance under communication disruption. After that, the POD parameter settings are carefully tuned, where the time delay and estimation error are considered, formulated as stability constraints using Razumikhin theorem, and solved via linear matrix inequality (LMI), yielding multi-dimensional robustness of the system, including operating conditions, time delay and communication disruption. Case studies in the improved 4-machine 2-area system and IEEE 39-bus system show that the proposed method can accurately estimate the state-space modeling of closed-loop system and effectively dampen power oscillations in time delay and communication disruption scenarios.

title: Degradation-Aware Real-Time Power Allocation Approach for Heterogeneous BESS
abstract: With growing hybrid configurations and phased deployments, rising heterogeneity in battery energy storage system (BESS) challenges the cost-minimization power allocation due to the difficulty in accurately quantifying realtime degradation cost. To address this, we propose a dual energy distribution model which stores the cycle information related to SoC trajectories within the energy distribution, tackling the problem to seek the full cycle for current action with past operation. A real-time degradation cost calculation formulation is presented to analytically express nonlinear degradation over a continuous action space, without requiring historical SoC backtracking or the rainflow simulation. A real-time power allocation algorithm is designed based on dual energy distribution ranking. Unlike traditional rainflowbased online methods that rely on estimating the marginal degradation cost of infinitesimal actions, our approach allocates power based on the degradation cost evaluated across the entire power range of each battery. Numerical tests and comparison are done for heterogeneous BESS response to frequency regulation service, the results show our method reduces daily degradation costs by 12% to 31% compared to conventional strategies, and with fast solving speed of each response within milliseconds.

title: Small-Signal Stability Assessment and Enhancement of Grid-Following/Grid-Forming Hybrid Systems Based on Voltage and Current Strength
abstract: With the rapid development of renewable energy, power systems are witnessing an increasing penetration of power converters. Currently, converters widely employ grid-following (GFL) control, while grid-forming (GFM) control is considered as a grid-friendly strategy to accommodate large-scale power converters. Hence, GFL-GFM hybrid systems (GGHSs) will prevail in the future. However, such systems may encounter small-signal stability issues across a wide frequency range due to the closed-loop interactions among the power network, GFL, and GFM converters. To address this problem, this paper first introduces the concept of grid current strength, a metric that quantitatively characterizes the stability of GFM converters, thereby extending the traditional grid voltage strength. We derive low-dimensional GFL and GFM subsystems to represent the dynamics and stability of the original high-dimensional system. On this basis, a two-dimensional strength index is proposed to quantitatively assess the stability margin of the GGHSs in a tractable manner. Based on this index, we analyze the impact of the proportions of GFL and GFM converters on system stability and demonstrate that inappropriate proportions may lead to instability. Finally, we propose a method to rapidly identify the critical GFL or GFM devices that dominate the system stability using participation factors. On this basis, we introduce stability enhancement strategies for GGHSs in both the system planning and system operational stages. The efficacy of the proposed assessment and enhancement methods is validated through time-domain simulations and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) tests.

title: Preventive Control Optimization Against Voltage Oscillations Induced by Steady-State Repeated LVRT Based on Thevenin Equivalent Parameter Correction
abstract: Accelerated global energy transition towards low carbon sources drives large-scale renewable integration, posing challenges to energy system security. In multi-renewable energy plants grid-connected systems (MREP-GCSs), repeated low voltage ride-through (LVRT) under steady-state can induce a novel switching oscillation. The oscillation stems from a self-sustaining cycle where, during steady-state operation, under certain grid conditions, increased active power output can trigger LVRT entry, which restores voltage and prompts LVRT exit, only for power restoration to immediately re-trigger the condition, causing persistent switching oscillations. Therefore, an optimized preventive control method is proposed against repeated LVRT, explicitly considering inter-plant influences in MREP-GCSs. Firstly, an assessment framework based on refined repeated LVRT occurrence conditions is developed. The re-derivation of this condition is based on equivalent parameters at the point of common coupling (PCC), considering the mutual power-voltage coupling between plants to correct the equivalent voltage. Secondly, a preventive control optimization method for repeated LVRT is developed from the perspective of online preventive control. To achieve precise regulation, a quantitative relationship between system-wide regulation variables combination and repeated LVRT boundary is established, along with other operating conditions, to form the constraints of the optimization model. The objective function aims to minimize regulation costs by coordinating grid-side and plant-side controls. This system-level method addresses the multi-plant boundary effects of control variables for coordinated multi-PCC control, optimizing grid plant co-regulation to ensure renewable energy accommodation and enhance stability. Simulation results demonstrate the method accurately identifies repeated LVRT scenarios and suppresses oscillations.

title: Optimal Configuration of HVAC Transmission With Mid-Cable Reactance Compensation for Far-Offshore Wind Farms
abstract: The feasible transmission distance of offshore wind farms (OWFs) connected via high-voltage alternating current (HVAC) systems can be significantly extended through mid-cable reactance compensation. This paper investigates the effectiveness of such compensation and proposes an integrated methodology for optimizing HVAC transmission configurations. First, analytical expressions for voltage and current profiles along the submarine cable with mid-cable reactance are derived, providing the foundation for identifying the key constraints that limit the maximum transmission capacity (MTC). Then, an optimization model based on the DistFlow model is developed, incorporating the cable’s capacitive effects. The model is formulated as a second-order cone program (SOCP), enabling accurate evaluation of the MTC in terms of rated power and transmission distance. Furthermore, a techno-economic evaluation framework is established to compare the break-even distances of various schemes, using the annualized equivalent cost (AEC) method that integrates capital investment, operation, and maintenance costs. The results show that mid-cable compensation can extend the break-even distance of HVAC systems by 10 to 100 km across different OWF capacities, thereby enhancing their suitability for far-offshore deployment. A sensitivity analysis is also performed to identify key cost drivers. Overall, the proposed approach supports optimal reactance compensation design and the selection of cost-effective HVAC transmission solutions for OWFs.

title: Improved PV System Control Strategies to Reduce Power Management Costs in Nanogrids
abstract: An improved PV system control method is proposed to reduce nanogrid operation costs in this paper. A model including it various components such as photovoltaic (PV) systems, energy storage systems (ESSs), gateways, and household loads is considered with the constraints of the ESS, PV irradiance from real data, and household load. We designed an optimal economic dispatch strategy with an improved PV system control method. Combining the proposed optimal economic dispatch and PV system control strategies, it can improve the control performance for both transient and steady-state responses thereby enabling the maximum power to be extracted from the PV. Consequently, the PV power is maximized, which allows the ESS to use less power and sell the surplus to external power sources, which means the proposed method decreases the nanogrid operation costs. This performance is verified via nanogrid simulations and PV experimental kit.

title: Privacy-Preserving Collaborative Assessment of Multi-Day Operation Security in Distribution Systems With High Levels of PV Penetration
abstract: A distribution system with high levels of photovoltaic (PV) penetration is greatly affected by possible prolonged abnormal weather events that may last for multi-days and thus invite multi-day coupling insecure operation issues. Also concerning that the utility distribution grid (UDG) and microgrids (MGs) in a distribution system are owned and managed by different stockholders, the paper presents a privacy-preserving collaborative assessment method for the system’s multi-day operational security. First, we characterize the multi-day evolution of PVs’ and loads’ forecast uncertainties by the customized martingale-like process. Then, we embed gradually increasing uncertainties in the coming days into the multi-day collaborative assessment model, whose optimistic and pessimistic decisions comprehensively indicate the respective normal, abnormal, or emergency states of networked UDG and MGs. Further, we formulate unified dual cuts and feasibility restoration cuts in the pessimistic case and optimistic case with respect to the mixed integer nature of UDG and MGs’ assessment model, by which the collaborative decisions can be made in a decentralized way without disclosing privacy. The optimal convergence of decentralized decision-making and the effectiveness of relaxation for binary variables are proven in mathematics. Finally, the experiment demonstrates that on the promise of privacy preservation, the proposed method is not only correctness and timeliness but also scalable and robust.

title: Energy Maximization Control of a Wave Energy Converter With a Switching Power Take-off
abstract: This paper presents a numerical optimal control method that can efficiently handle the complexities brought by switching power take-offs (PTOs) commonly used in wave energy converters (WECs). Switching PTOs allow large flywheels to be attached to the generator, which help maintain unidirectional generator motion while not causing significant reduction in the speed of the prime mover. This flexibility enables similar levels of wave energy capture with a larger generator inertia value, which can smooth generator velocity peaks and lead to lower-rated components. Developed based on the principle of dynamic programming (DP), the proposed method simultaneously computes optimal switching instants and optimal generator torque, combining discrete decisions and continuous trajectory optimization in a single framework. The computational complexity is greatly reduced compared to standard DP processes through critical assumptions and partial analytical solutions. This method is applied to an oscillating surge WEC model with realistic parameters obtained from previous experiments. Simulation results show an increase of more than 15% in captured wave energy just by replacing the conventional linear PTO with a switching one, which increases active energy by inducing larger motion. Increasing the flywheel inertia attached to the generator slightly decreases captured energy, but significantly reduces generator velocity peaks.

title: A Data-Driven Dynamic Temporal Correlation Modeling Framework for Renewable Energy Scenario Generation
abstract: The temporal correlation of renewable energy generation is inherently influenced by atmospheric systems. To capture its time-varying characteristics, a data-driven modeling framework is proposed for short-term renewable energy scenario generation. The framework uses a decoupled mapping approach to separately model marginal distributions and the correlation structure, with accuracy ensured through optimization based on proper scoring rules. The scenario generation process consists of two stages. In the first stage, a dynamic correlation network adaptively models temporal correlations by updating the covariance matrix, providing a more interpretable representation compared to traditional generative models. In the second stage, an implicit quantile network models the marginal quantile function in a nonparametric, continuous manner, enabling scenario generation through marginal inverse sampling. Experimental results show that the proposed dynamic correlation quantile network outperforms state-of-the-art methods in quantifying uncertainty and capturing dynamic temporal correlation.

title: Virtual Inertia Limit Estimation Method for Power Systems with High Proportion of Renewable Energy Considering Time Delay
abstract: As the increasing capacity of renewable energy sources (RESs), power system with high RES penetration urgently need virtual inertia support from RESs. Current research has found that, due to inherent time delay, providing excessive virtual inertia from RESs may instead cause small-signal instability in the power system. Therefore, determining the upper limit of virtual inertia from RESs is critical to ensuring small-signal stability. However, current studies have only proposed methods for determining small-signal stability in power systems that consider VIC time delay, with limited discussion of the upper limit of virtual inertia. Therefore, a discrete system frequency response (SFR) model considering VIC time delay is established in this paper. It is found through analysis that the frequency sampling period affects the critical stability condition much more sensitively than the time delay length. Furthermore, a sufficient condition for small-signal stability is proposed, which describes the upper limit of the virtual inertia of RESs by the frequency sampling period and the system inertia time constant. Although this condition is a conservative estimation of the upper limit of virtual inertia, but the experiment on the test bench of wind-integrated power systems verifies that the sufficient condition is close to the critical condition. The sufficient condition is independent of the time delay length, making it more suitable for guiding practical engineering applications.

title: Small-Signal Security Region of Floating Offshore Wind Turbine under Wind and Wave Disturbances
abstract: The wind and wave disturbances of floating offshore wind turbine (FOWT) present significant challenges for small-signal security analysis, due to the nonlinear aero-hydro dynamics and variable working points. This paper proposes a mechanical-electrical coupling FOWT model and analyzes its stability under wind and wave disturbances, deriving the stable operating area. The model incorporates both the mechanical torque applied to the generator and the electrical torque of the generator affects the mechanical dynamics. Compared with a fixed-bottom wind turbine (FWT), new oscillation modes are revealed for the linearized FOWT model to analyze its stability. Based on the FOWT model, the small-signal security region (SSSR) is formulated, offering a geometric representation of the stability boundaries under wind and wave injection space. Due to the coupling characteristics of FOWTs, new dominant oscillation modes leading to Hopf bifurcation on the SSSR boundary are observed, compared with FWT model. Simulations of the proposed model on the single machine infinite system (SMIB) and the four-area system derive the SSSR boundary under wind and wave disturbances, validating the proposed model and SSSR derivation method.

title: Model Order Reduction of DFWTs Based Wind Power System With Inhomogeneous Initial Condition
abstract: Although model order reduction based on balanced truncation (BT) has excellent performance in preserving accurate output of doubly-fed wind turbine based wind power system (DFWT-WPS), these applications are usually based on zero-initial condition. However, due to the inhomogeneous initial condition caused by soft-starting operation, the direct application of BT will lead to large response deviation. Therefore, this paper presents a method to construct the reduced order model of DFWT-WPS considering inhomogeneous initial condition, while reserving advantages of BT. Firstly, the system output is decomposed into two independent system outputs according to Duhamel principle. The first system contains zero-initial condition with input (standard BT model, SBTM) and the second system contains inhomogeneous initial condition without input. Secondly, the second system is converted into an equivalent one with dirac delta function as the input and zeroinitial condition (SBTM). Then, the two SBTMs are applied BT and the outputs are superimposed to get the reduced order response of the DFWT-WPS. One step further, the accurate upper bound of the error between the reduced order system and the original one is derived. Finally, the paper takes 20 /60 /120 DFWTs in parallel under different wind speed conditions as examples to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method with inhomogeneous initial condition.

title: Advanced Flexible Solar Interconnection into Distribution Systems with Dynamic Asset Rating and Fail-Safe Mode Control
abstract: Avangrid piloted the first Flexible Interconnection (Flex IX) project in North America with two sites running for 4 years. Lessons learned from these pilot projects showed that solar farms can experience measurable curtailment due to overloading of grid assets based on their static thermal limits in normal grid operation and the fail-safe (FS) mode control of solar generation output during loss of communication (LOC) contingencies. To address these issues, the paper proposed two advanced Flex IX technologies, i.e., (1) dynamic asset rating (DAR) and (2) enhanced FS mode control by dynamically configuring DER controllers. DAR is to holistically update thermal ratings of grid assets, i.e., substation transformers (Xfmrs) and feeder conductors, in Flex IX by leveraging real-time meteorological measurements. Advanced short-term load forecasting based on Multivariate Linear Regression, TSMixer and Reservoir Computing has been proposed to update the curtailment configurations of Flex IX controllers when communication outages occur. These developed technologies have been validated with the data from the Flex IX sites from Avangrid. Results show that DAR reduces solar curtailment by 23.89% in the synthetic case and by 100% in the Flex IX demonstration site. And the improved FS mode reduces communication outage related solar curtailment by 76.48% in the synthetic case and by 100% for the Flex IX demonstration site.

title: Disturbance Observer-Based Model Reference Adaptive Control for Inertia Control of Unknown-Inertia Power Grids
abstract: Existing studies on inertia control depend on knowing or estimating the grid equivalent inertia when renewable energy sources (RESs) are present. To eliminate the need for accurate knowledge or estimate of the grid equivalent inertia, this paper proposes employing the battery energy storage system (BESS) to inject inertia into the grid when RESs are connected to the grid, maintaining the original grid inertia—essentially the value without zero-inertia resources. This is accomplished by designing a model reference adaptive control (MRAC) scheme that uses the power system inertia without zero-inertia resources as a reference to determine the inertia that the BESS must inject. To this end, disturbance observer (DOB)-based MRAC is proposed and integrated into the BESS droop control loop. The DOB estimates load changes based on frequency deviations, and the MRAC uses this information to adjust the BESS output power, ensuring the system inertia and frequency reach the reference. Since the performance of the DOB affects the model reference adaptive controller, the steps to designing the DOB and proper tuning of the adaptation gain, which yields fast dynamics and satisfactory results, are laid out. Moreover, a novel approach is presented for enabling participation of multiple BESSs in inertia control. Real-time simulations are carried out to verify the efficacy of the proposed method in maintaining the grid inertia, and thus the system frequency, around the desired value.

title: A Novel Active Shadow-Based Fault Detection and Localization Method for Photovoltaic Systems
abstract: Fault detection in photovoltaic (PV) systems is crucial for operation safety. However, traditional methods often struggle with accurately identifying and locating faults under normal operation and require complex sensor setups. To enhance the efficiency and accuracy of fault detection and localization, this study proposes an active shadow (AS)-based fault detection method for PV systems. By introducing an active shading device to the PV modules and applying shadows in a specific sequence, the method analyzes changes in array output power to accurately detect and locate faults, enabling rapid fault detection without disrupting normal operation. Through introducing a multi-level high-precision simulation model based on the series substrings and defining an identification coefficient (IC) to evaluate the algorithm’s performance, this method is proved to locate faults across various PV array sizes under complex partial shading (with varying shadow areas, positions and intensities), as well as short-circuit and open-circuit faults. Real-world PV array experiments further confirm the method’s feasibility and robustness.

title: Lyapunov Compatibility-Based Adaptive Consensus Algorithm in PV-BESS Integrated Island DC Microgrids: A Dynamic State of Charge Balancing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel State-of-Charge (SoC)- based power allocation strategy for photovoltaic (PV)-based DC microgrids, leveraging an adaptive consensus algorithm to ensure SoC balance across Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) nodes. The primary control scheme employs inner-loop current droop control to mitigate disturbances arising from PV operation. The SoC-based power allocation strategy serves as a secondary control mechanism, designed to maintain a uniform SoC level across all BESS nodes via the adaptive consensus algorithm. This algorithm is compatible with a range of secondary control types, thereby mitigating battery degradation. Specifically, the stability and compatibility of the SoC-based power allocation strategy are rigorously proven by constructing a Lyapunov function. The proposed control strategy is simulated in MATLAB/SIMULINK and in an OPAL-RT-based real-time simulation environment to demonstrate its effectiveness, in which the proposed adaptive consensus algorithm can accommodate two different secondary control strategies.

title: Accurate and Computationally Efficient Aggregated Modelling of Offshore Wind Farms for Grid Compliance
abstract: Detailed electromagnetic transient models of off shore wind farms incorporate the individual wind turbine dynamics and controls of many wind turbines (WTs), resulting in substantial computational burdens. This limits their practicality for large-scale system studies. While aggregation techniques re duce this burden, they often compromise accuracy, particularly in capturing dynamic behaviour during power system disturbances. To overcome this challenge, this paper proposes a gaussian mixture model clustering with information-theoretic averaging to group similar WTs and derive representative aggregated models. A structured eigenvalue sensitivity analysis is conducted to identify the control parameters that have the greatest impact on system dynamics, reducing the dimensionality of the parameter space. Additionally, an improved multi-objective gradient descent optimisation strategy is developed to identify and provide optimal values of system and control parameters under varying wind conditions and fault scenarios to ensure accuracy. The proposed modelling applicability is further demonstrated through assessment on an HVDC connected offshore wind farm under large disturbance and weak grid conditions in the time and frequency domains. Finally, the aggregated model's performance is validated against the detailed benchmark to ensure UK's grid compliance on modelling, confirming its ability to replicate key dynamic and steady-state characteristics with substantially reduced computational effort.

title: A Bi-Level Robust Energy Storage Siting and Sizing Model of Distribution System With Energy Affordability Enforced
abstract: The energy affordability principles aim to enhance energy accessibility and reduce electricity expenditures for low-income communities. However, the advocated affordability policies impose new requirements on system operators, as few have been translated into technical utility models. Energy storage systems (ESS) are crucial in implementing energy affordability by regulating voltage profiles and reducing power loss. This paper proposes an energy affordability-embedded robust planning (EARP) model to relieve the energy burden of low-income loads through equitable ESS deployment. The proposed model innovatively enforces implicit energy affordability (EA) constraints into technical models with two steps. First, an energy affordability slackness component (EASC) variable is introduced to evaluate the smallest gaps between the given preliminary planning decisions and the desired affordability-satisfied decisions. Then, by relaxing the dispatch model with the EASC variable, the implicit EA constraints are converted into explicitly cutting planes using the duality theorem. The proposed bi-level EARP model is solved via an improved column & constraint generation (C&CG) algorithm. Case studies on the IEEE 33-Bus and 123-Bus systems verify the model's effectiveness in relieving energy burdens and achieving better sustainability in the long term compared with conventional bill assistance programs.

title: Flexibilizing Grid-Connected Renewable Power to Ammonia Systems via a Novel Hydrogen Storage Design: Configuration and Operational Strategy
abstract: Renewable power to ammonia (ReP2A) offers a promising route for renewable energy utilization. To fully utilize volatile renewable generation without breaking process continuity, ReP2A systems require hydrogen storage subsystems with storage tanks and compressors. However, the conventional layout of hydrogen storage subsystems can cause significant hydrogen supply pressure variations, restricting the ReP2A system to a semi-steady-state operation inadequate for handling renewable fluctuations. In practice, feedforward control based on shortterm forecasts is widely employed, yet forecast errors necessitate substantial grid electricity purchases to maintain continuity. This coupling between power and chemical manufacturing increases grid peak-shaving pressure and undermines economic benefits. To address these challenges, a novel hydrogen storage subsystem with a parallel-connected compressor is proposed to enhance pressure regulation, alongside a capacity allocation method and a state-transition-based PID (ST-PID) control strategy. Furthermore, a multi-timescale framework embeds the ST-PID controller to bridge real-time control and long-term optimization. Case studies with real-world data demonstrate that the proposed system unlocks the flexibility for renewable consumption and shows robustness against prediction errors, reducing grid electricity reliance by 38.56% and lowering the levelized cost of ammonia by 8.75%. This offers dual benefits in promoting renewable integration and enhancing economic performance.

title: Regular Layout Optimization for Offshore Wind Farms Considering Seabed Terrains and Turbulence Intensity
abstract: The offshore wind farm layout optimization (OWFLO) is critical to effectively reducing energy costs. This study presents a planning method for the regular layout of OWF, considering both seabed terrains and turbulence intensity (TI), which is based on a mixed-integer linear fractional programming (MILFP) model. The proposed model considers the life-cycle costs of OWFs, including support structure costs, installation costs, and operation and maintenance (O&M) costs, in which the objective function aims to minimize the levelized cost of energy (LCOE). To address the computational challenges of large-scale OWFLO, we utilize the regular layouts' “patterns” to reduce the dimensions of decision variables and simplify the power calculation constraints, so that the model can be decomposed and solved by the Bounded Dinkelbach Algorithm (BDA). Finally, the applicability of the proposed model on different terrains is validated through a real OWF in China.

title: Real-Time Voltage Control in Smart Distribution Network Through Multi-Agent Cooperative Optimization
abstract: With the increasing renewable energy penetration, maintaining real-time voltage stability becomes increasingly challenging for smart distribution networks due to the stochastic nature of distributed generation and loads. To address this, a fully cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework is proposed for distributed voltage control under uncertainty. The problem is formulated as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), where each controllable node operates as an agent with local observations. A security-region-based policy optimization scheme is introduced to adapt control objectives across different voltage ranges. A cooperation advantage function is embedded in the policy update to guide agents toward globally beneficial actions. Additionally, a joint action-value function incorporating a cooperation metric is designed to promote inter-agent coordination during training, particularly under varying volatility across renewable and load nodes. The framework adopts centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE) paradigm, with daily operation modeled as a training episode. The proposed method is validated on two modified single-phase networks and two unbalanced three-phase distribution network. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves robust and stable real-time voltage regulation while enhancing overall system cooperation.

title: Pre-Trained Large Model as Distributed PV Power Forecaster: Integrating Scenario-Consistent Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Cross-Modal Semantic Alignment
abstract: The rapid proliferation of distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems presents significant challenges for accurate power generation forecasting due to their inherent intermittency and spatial-temporal variability. This paper proposes a novel framework that leverages pre-trained large models for distributed PV power forecasting by integrating retrieval-augmented generation with cross-modal semantic alignment. To unlock the reasoning capabilities of pre-trained large models, we design a scenario-consistent RAG module that retrieves relevant historical PV sequences guided by long-term dependencies and temporal correlations, and integrates them through a Chain-of-Thought prompting paradigm. Furthermore, we develop a cross-modal semantic alignment mechanism to bridge the representational gap between numerical PV series data and the language semantic space of PLMs, enabling effective pattern recognition across modalities. To ensure physically meaningful forecasting within the training and inference processes, we also establish a constrained activation function that explicitly considers the inherent characteristics of PV power generation. Extensive experiments on nine real-world distributed PV datasets demonstrate that our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming six benchmark models.

title: Fast Active Power Reduction Based Fault Ride-Through Control Strategy for VSC-HVDC Integrating Offshore Wind Farm Under Onshore Fault
abstract: The voltage source converter-based high voltage direct current (VSC-HVDC) integrating offshore wind farm (OWF) system suffers from direct current (DC) overvoltage under onshore grid fault. The existing methods mainly use DC chopper of VSC-HVDC or voltage drop control of the OWF to mitigate DC overvoltage, which lead to high costs or forced tripping of offshore wind turbine generators (WTGs). To suppress DC overvoltage and promote active power recovery, this paper proposes a two-stage fast active power reduction (FAPR) based fault ride-through control strategy. By mathematically clarifying the FAPR capacity of the WTG, the DC chopper resistances of the WTG and VSC-HVDC are economically designed. Then, during stage 1, a scheme that combines FAPR control of the OWF with DC chopper control of VSC-HVDC is proposed to suppresses DC overvoltage. During stage 2, considering the issue of electromagnetic torque saturation when offshore WTGs undergo fast active power recovery, a fast pitch angle reduction control scheme is proposed to facilitate the active power recovery. Simulations and experiments validate that the proposed method avoids DC overvoltage. Besides, the DC chopper resistors are reduced by 90% and 80% compared with DC chopper-based method and voltage drop-based method, respectively.

title: Bridging Market Efficiency and System Resilience: Unified Multi-Service Operation of Long-Duration Energy Storage in Decarbonized Power Systems
abstract: The rapid growth of variable renewable generation and the increasing frequency of extreme events demand power systems that are both economical and resilient. Long-duration energy storage (LDES) stands out as a unique solution, capable of shifting energy across multiple days while providing critical support during large-scale outages. However, our review of existing approaches highlights critical gaps: market operations and system restoration are typically optimized in isolation, and the technology-specific characteristics of LDES make their coordinated use especially challenging. We first investigate these challenges, including efficiency-capacity trade-offs, duration mismatches, and restoration-sequence dependencies, and underscore the need for an integrated framework. To address this gap, this paper introduces a unified multi-service optimization model that co-optimizes LDES for both economic and resilience objectives within a single mixed-integer linear program. The formulation combines energy arbitrage, capacity adequacy, and renewable integration with resilience metrics based on avoided unserved energy and a priority-based restoration mechanism capturing spatiotemporal re-energization and progressive load pickup. Multi-objective Pareto analysis reveals cost-resilience trade-offs, providing actionable insights for system planners. To demonstrate technology-agnostic applicability, the model is applied to two contrasting LDES technologies, hydrogen (H$_{2}$) and flow battery (FB), on a benchmark test system with seasonal PV and load profiles under diverse blackout scenarios. Simulation results show that the proposed framework reduces operating costs in normal conditions while accelerating critical-load recovery and system-wide restoration after disruptions, advancing the state-of-the-art in storage-integrated power system operation.

title: Reactive Power Coordination Control to Enhance Weak Grid Stability of Hybrid Power Plants
abstract: The rise of inverter-based resources (IBRs) and the retirement of synchronous generators weaken modern power systems by lowering the system strength. This leads to a lower short-circuit ratio ($SCR$) at the point of common coupling (PCC) of IBR facilities, resulting in weak grid conditions that hinder power transfer and threaten angle stability. To prevent angle instability, maintaining the PCC voltage at $1\:pu$ or higher is crucial, but injecting high active power into weak grids often increases the PCC voltage due to the high coupling impedance. Conventional voltage droop control ($QV-$droop) supplies reactive power by reducing the voltage at PCC, and compromises angle stability and contradicts the voltage requirement in weak grids. Hybrid power plants (HPPs), which combine grid-forming IBRs (like energy storage) and grid-following IBRs (like wind/solar), can enhance angle stability and ensure power transfer in weak grids. This study presents a dynamic reactive power sharing strategy at the plant level that uses GFM IBRs for PCC voltage control and GFL IBRs for reactive power support. The proposed algorithm was validated through EMT Simulations, demonstrating its efficacy under weak grid conditions.

title: A Weight-Allocation and Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning Approach for the BTM PV Power Forecasting
abstract: Distributed ultra-short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting plays a vital role in analyzing behind-the-meter (BTM) solar generation and enhancing grid stability. As federated learning (FL) is increasingly applied to distributed BTM PV forecasting on a large scale, its deployment is confronted with two major challenges, namely performance degradation arising from device heterogeneity and privacy risks associated with global communication. To address these challenges, a novel collaborative method, termed AWA-DDP-FL, is proposed, which integrates adaptive weight assignment (AWA) with reinforcement learning-driven dynamic differential privacy (DDP). Specifically, AWA mitigates the impact of device heterogeneity by strategically excluding underperforming clients and dynamically adjusting local model aggregation weights during training. Meanwhile, DDP enables each distributed PV client to autonomously adjust its privacy budget in real time according to data sensitivity, balancing privacy protection and model performance through dynamic noise injection. Experimental results on real-world PV datasets show that the proposed method obtains normalized root mean square error of 5.110% and normalized mean absolute error of 2.630%, indicating that the proposed algorithm achieves higher accuracy even under noise perturbations.

title: RoCoF Constrained Regional Inertia Security Region: Formulation and Application
abstract: The regional inertia, which determines the regional rate of change of frequency (RoCoF), should be kept in a secure status in renewable-penetrated power systems. To break away from mapping the regional maximum RoCoF with regional inertia in a linearized form, this paper comprehensively studies the regional inertia security problem from formulation to applications. Firstly, the regional inertia security region (R-ISR) is defined, whose boundary is non-linear and non-convex. Then, a local linearized method is devised to calculate the global maximum of regional RoCoF. The non-convex ISR boundary is expressed by multiple simple boundaries corresponding to each local solution, which can be obtained by a simple search-based method. Finally, the convexified R-ISR constraint is formed by convex decomposition and embedded in an inertia optimal adjustment model. The results on 3-region systems show some counter-intuitive findings, such as increasing the inertia of one region may worsen its RoCoF.

title: Interpretable Wind Power Forecasting With Feature and Loss Function Construction Guided by Domain Knowledge
abstract: Current wind power forecasting (WPF) methods predominantly rely on data-driven deep learning models, inherently lacking integration of domain knowledge, which limits forecasting accuracy and model interpretability. To address this issue, an interpretable data-knowledge fusion ultra-short-term WPF model is proposed, in which domain knowledge guides the feature construction process and is directly embedded into the design of the loss function. In the feature construction module, a wind speed-power curve is established to generate theoretical power outputs by using historical wind speed as inputs. These theoretical outputs, combined with historical measured data, serve as inputs for the model. In the loss function construction module, a boundary constraint loss is designed by extracting the upper and lower boundaries of wind power output using the alpha shape algorithm and Local Weighted Linear Regression based on wind speed and power data. Notably, the parameters of boundaries are dynamically updated to capture the volatility of wind power. Additionally, an error distribution shape loss is introduced to penalize the deviation of the training error distribution from the normal distribution, using Jensen-Shannon divergence as an indicator. Case studies across 30 wind farms demonstrate that the proposed method guided by interpretable knowledge achieves the best average performance across all time horizons compared to baseline models. The method also shows strong robustness in noise and missing data experiments.

title: Less-Conservative Current Feasible Region for PLL-Synchronized VSCs Considering Variable Damping Under Asymmetric Faults
abstract: During low voltage ride through (LVRT) period, variable damping significantly affects the transient synchronous stability (TSS) of phase-locked loop-synchronized voltage-source converters (PLL-VSCs). However, in previous studies on TSS analysis under asymmetric faults, completely ignoring and insufficiently considering variable damping both increase the misjudging risk or yielding conservative estimation results. To fill this gap, this paper proposes an improved equal area criterion (iEAC) considering variable damping to qualitatively analyze the TSS of PLL-VSC and quantitatively estimate the less-conservatism current feasible region under asymmetric faults. Firstly, the sequence-domain transient synchronization model with PLL dynamics is developed to reveal the synchronization characteristics of PLL-VSC. Then, an improved equal area criterion considering variable damping is proposed to qualitatively analyze the effect of variable damping on TSS. Compared to traditional methods, the proposed iEAC improves both accuracy and conservatism on TSS analysis. Moreover, an iterative estimation method based on the iEAC is put forward to construct a less-conservatism sequence-domain current feasible region (SCFR), which provides a quantitative design for current injections under asymmetric faults to achieve system LVRT. The expansion feasibility of the proposed modeling and TSS analysis method to the multi-VSCs system is fully discussed. Finally, hardware-in-loop experiments validate the effectiveness and superiority of the theoretical analysis.

title: Integrated Driving Method to Optimize Operation of Wind Turbines for Weakening the Wake Effect
abstract: The wake effect in wind farms (WFs) leads to wind energy loss and increases the fatigue load of wind turbines (WTs). In this paper, an integrated driving method (IDM) to optimize operation of wind turbines (WTs) for weakening the wake effect. Considering the wake effect with delayed time, a model predicted control (MPC)-based WT control method is proposed to optimize the dual-parameter, i.e., pitch angle and generator torque, for mitigating fatigue load and increasing power generation. To pursue the better optimization effect, the data-driven method (DDM) is proposed to learn the accurate and complete dataset for eliminating linearization errors in the nonlinear physical of wind turbines and engineering wake models. DDM is designed to capture the nonlinear aerodynamic interactions based on the operational status of WTs in wake-affected WFs. It utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based encoder and a graph neural network (GNN)-based decoder. Subsequently, an artificial neural network (ANN)-based fusion method is proposed to select the better optimization values of these two methods for improving the prediction reliability and anti-measurement noise interference ability. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed scheme is substantiated through case studies involving a wake-affected WF.

title: Optimal Planning of Offshore Wind Farm Collector System considering Intensive Sea Use
abstract: Driven by the global clean energy transition, the offshore wind power has been expanding rapidly worldwide. In offshore wind farms (OWFs), the electrical collector system (ECS) already accounts for a substantial portion of the total project cost, while emerging sea-use regulations call for compact, corridor-based cable layouts instead of traditional dispersed radial schemes. This paper proposes an OWF-ECS planning framework tailored to the intensive use of sea areas. We for mulate a mixed-integer linear programming model (MILP) that incorporates the requirement of the intensive sea-use and uses the parallel-laying length of cables to represent spatial intensification. A clustering-based warm-start strategy and distance based candidate-arc reduction are further designed to improve solution efficiency and scalability. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed framework can accommodate diverse sea-use requirements and intensification levels, consistently generating economically efficient and spatially intensive ECS layouts and obtaining high-quality feasible or optimal solutions within acceptable computation time.

title: Analysis of External Short-Circuit Fault Characteristics and Safety Impact in PEMFC System Integrated With Renewable Energy
abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFC) integrated with renewable energy sources face risks from external electrical short-circuit (ESC) faults. ESC faults not only threaten the power system side but also adversely impact internal physical parameters, such as temperature and gas diffusion. The resulting abnormal dynamics of internal physical quantities (e.g., thermal and gas conditions) within the PEMFC stack can affect safe and reliable system operation. However, little research focuses on the characteristics of external electrical faults and their multi-physics impact on the internal response of PEMFC systems. Therefore, this paper first analyzes the external electrical characteristics and internal multi-physics response of PEMFCs after an ESC fault, using an equivalent circuit model of the PEMFC system integrated with renewables. On this basis, this paper proposes a method to evaluate the safe operation boundary of the studied system post-ESC fault, considering PEMFC internal temperature and gas safety limits. Finally, the analysis is verified on simulation and experimental platforms, and key operating factors are investigated. Experimental and simulation results show excellent agreement, with an error of less than 1%, demonstrating the method’s effectiveness for safety analysis. The results indicate that clearing faults within minutes can prevent membrane thermal damage. This research provides valuable theoretical insights for developing safe operation strategies for the PEMFC system in renewable energy integration.

title: Stability Boundary Analysis for Grid-Following (GFL) and Grid-Forming (GFM) Inverters
abstract: Studying the dynamics and stability of inverter-driven power systems has become a top priority for grid operators in view of the massive renewable energy deployment. The simplest and most widely used model for stability analysis for such networks is the single-inverter single- bus (SISB) equivalent model. Although quite insightful, SISB models with an L-filter for the inverter suffer from implementation difficulties due to algebraic loops. This paper develops a closed-form SISB model for grid-following (GFL) and grid-forming (GFM) inverters and derives symbolic formulation for the linearized system, which resolves algebraic loops and obtains fast results with uncompromised precision. This model is then used in an N-Dimensional Stability Boundary Tracking (ND-SBT) algorithm, which identifies the stability boundary for GFL and GFM inverters. This is the first method to infer the stability region for an arbitrary number of dimensions in a computationally efficient and software-agnostic manner while preserving accuracy. A detailed sensitivity analysis yields useful findings on the stability impact of individual parameters, while the results are validated using the IEEE 14- bus system.

title: Improved Reachability Analysis for VSC-MTDC Integrated Offshore Wind Farms Based on Adaptive Parameter Optimization
abstract: To address the challenges presented by the complex nonlinear dynamics and limited disturbance resilience of offshore wind farms (OWFs) integrated via voltage source converter based multi-terminal high voltage direct current (VSC-MTDC) system under large disturbances, an improved reachability analysis method is proposed to capture dynamic behaviors of the system. The analysis framework encompasses: 1) high-dimensional nonlinear differential and hybrid models of VSC-MTDC integrated OWFs system are constructed based on Kron reduction method to enhance computational efficiency and mitigate the limitations imposed by algebraic constraints; 2) an adaptive time-step optimization algorithm is implemented to further improve computational efficiency while enhancing the capability to capture both transient and steady-state dynamics of hybrid system; 3) the improved reachability algorithm is designed to quantitatively analyze the operational states of VSC-MTDC integrated OWFs system under uncertainties and varying operating conditions. Case studies on VSC-MTDC integrated OWFs system are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in revealing complex nonlinear characteristics and safety verification under large disturbances.

title: A Real-Time Blockchain Enabled Digital Twin Framework With Energy Trading Estimation for Optimized Management in a Virtual Power Plant
abstract: This work presents a novel digital twin (DT) framework integrated with blockchain to ensure real-time optimized energy management of virtual power plants (VPPs). The framework design leveragesenergy trading forecasts for both day-ahead scheduling and real-time operation in a VPP consisting of solar generation, battery storage, and grid supply. Key inputs include forecasted solar irradiance, load patterns, real time sensor readings, and historical data, while the twin outputs span optimized energy dispatch, battery State of Charge (SoC), grid voltage stability, energy transactions, and load profiles for all participants. All critical sensor data and energy trades are securely recorded on the blockchain ledger, enabling transparent verification of operations rather than directly implementing the model on the DT making the overall design lightweight and fast responding. The proposed framework has been implemented and tested in MATLAB-Simulink, with validation against physical system performance to evaluate its effectiveness in efficient energy management. Experimental results show high fidelity between the twin and the physical VPP: real-time measurement discrepancies are essentially zero, with variances in RMS voltage close to 1 V and energy transactions remain below 2 W.

title: Medium-Frequency Oscillation Analysis and Single-Parameter Feedback Suppression for Full-Size Converter-Based Variable-Speed Pumped Storage and Renewable Energy Combined System
abstract: The coordinated operation of the full-size converter-based variable-speed pumped storage unit (FSC-VSPSU) and renewable energy station can help smooth the power fluctuations and improve the renewable energy utilization. However, this combined system may encounter instability problem such as medium-frequency oscillation in practical application. The impedance-based analysis method is commonly used for addressing such instability problems. Nevertheless, existing research lacks an impedance model of FSC-VSPSU and does not fully conduct the stability analysis of the system. Hence, this paper develops the impedance model for FSC-VSPSU. By integrating it with the impedance model of renewable energy units, an equivalent impedance model of the entire system is derived. The system stability is then analyzed using the impedance-based analysis method. To address the instability issues, a suppression method based on a single feedback parameter k is proposed for FSC-VSPSU. This method reshapes the equivalent impedance with minimal complexity, eliminating the need for filters that typically degrade dynamic response performance in existing solutions. Simulation and experimental results are presented to validate the effectiveness of the established impedance model and the proposed control strategy.

title: A Current-Limiting Method based on Grid- Following Factor in a Virtual Synchronous Generator
abstract: The current-referencing electrified synchronous machine (CURESYM) is a virtual synchronous generator based on dual electromotive forces (EMFs), each of which is related to current regulation and synchronization, respectively. Since the synchronizing EMF (SEMF) is virtually decoupled from current regulation in CURESYMs, it needs to be appropriately managed during grid faults to strictly limit the entire output current. This article introduces a new concept called the grid-following factor to adjust the proximity of the SEMF with the grid voltage, along with a method for determining it to limit current instantaneously. The proposed method is demonstrated through various grid fault tests, with conditions based on publicly recognized standards regarding grid connection. The results confirm that the proposed method is effective in current limiting under both transient and steady-state conditions. Notably, the proposed method enhances voltage support via reactive power injection even during unbalanced faults, while simultaneously reducing the peak current within a predefined limit. Furthermore, the experimental validation using an actual power conversion setup corroborates the practical applicability of the proposed method.

title: Model Predictive Control Method for an Integrated Community Energy System Based on a GRU-Driven Dynamic Energy Hub
abstract: In integrated community energy systems (ICESs), the efficiency parameters of energy conversion devices are influenced not only by current operating conditions (e.g., device load rate, temperature, and atmospheric pressure) but also by the dynamic characteristics of historical operating conditions. Neglecting the nonlinear dynamic relationship between the efficiency parameters and time series operating conditions can notably reduce the prediction accuracy for the efficiency parameters, thereby disrupting the energy supply-demand balance and reducing the economic performance of the ICES. To address this issue, a model predictive control (MPC) method is proposed for an ICES based on a gated recurrent unit (GRU)-driven dynamic energy hub (G-DEH). First, a G-DEH model is developed to capture the time series correlations in the operating conditions of the ICES, thereby accurately modeling the nonlinear and time-varying relationships between the efficiency parameters and these conditions. On this basis, an optimal scheduling model for the ICES, focused on enhancing the economic performance, is developed via the G-DEH model. The model is subjected to iterative rolling calibration through the MPC strategy, dynamically adjusting the degree of matching between the operating conditions and efficiency parameters, thereby enhancing the adaptability of the scheduling model to complex and dynamic operating conditions. The simulation results from a case study demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms traditional methods in terms of the prediction accuracy for the efficiency parameters and the economic performance of the ICES. This confirms the significant value of the method in reducing operating costs and enhancing dynamic adaptability.

title: Voltage Deviation and Wideband Oscillation Constrained Stability and Weakness Analysis of Hybrid GFM/GFL Multi-Converter Systems
abstract: The oscillation risk assessment and oscillation source identification pose significant challenges for heterogeneous multi-converter systems such as hybrid grid forming and grid-following renewable energy station (GFM/GFL-RES). Furthermore, the theoretical impact of GFM converter capacity and placement on the voltage support strength and resonant modes of each bus remains unexplored. To fill this gap, this paper proposes a stability assessment and weakness location method for hybrid GFM/GFL multi-converter systems. Firstly, a power flow method incorporating the reactive power support capability of the GFM converter and the multiple renewable short-circuit ratio is used to evaluate the voltage support strength at each bus. Then, a s-domain modal analysis method incorporating frequency-coupling is proposed. This method accurately extracts system resonant modes by combining modal impedance curves and a center-difference Newton Raphson iterative algorithm. Finally, the steady-state stability region is established by integrating steady-state voltage stability and small-signal stability. The method in this paper is validated through a 16-converter 34-bus GFM/GFL-RES, and the influence of GFM capacity and placement on the steady-state stability region of the system is quantified. The accuracy of the proposed stability analysis method is verified by time-domain simulation.

title: Coordinated Fuzzy Active Power Control of Wind Turbines With Load Optimization
abstract: In modern power systems with a high penetration of wind energy, active power control (APC) enables wind turbines to track the power reference set by the control center. However, the rapidity and accuracy requirements of APC mode always lead to large fatigue loads of turbines' components. This paper proposes a set of fuzzy logic-based APC strategies integrated together to achieve the joint load optimization of key components while reducing power loss. Firstly, a lower bound parameter for pitch range limitation updated by rotor speed is created to realize a dynamic adjustment of the variable-speed range participating in active power tracking, effectively reducing the load of the pitch system. Secondly, a torque acceleration adjustment parameter is updated adaptively through the established fuzzy logic rules to optimize both acceleration and deceleration performance, thereby reducing power production loss when the available wind power is less than the desired reference. Furthermore, we design an upper bound parameter for pitch range limitation to find a load optimization trade-off among the pitch system, the drive train, and the blade root under high wind speed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed controllers is validated on a semi-physical hardware testing platform.

title: Decision-Oriented Dynamic Operating Envelopes for Distributed Energy Resources via End-to-End Learning With Simulation-in-the-Loop
abstract: The large-scale exploitation of distributed energy resources (DERs) has significantly enhanced the sustainability, flexibility, and cost efficiency of distribution networks. Dynamic operating envelopes (DOEs) provide a technically reliable and practical solution to ensure operational security and facilitate DER utilization. This paper proposes an end-to-end learning-based approach with simulation-in-the-loop (E2E-SiL) for optimizing the DOEs for DERs, which merits a decision-oriented training framework with excellent reliability and computational efficiency. An input convex neural network (ICNN) model is applied to estimate the mapping relationship from bus power injection to constraint violation while ensuring the convexity of analytical expressions for critical physical quantities in DOE optimization. Based on the ICNN model, the DOE optimization problem is transformed into a fully linear form solvable within seconds. To bridge the gap between theoretical DOE formulation and practical applications, simulation software is utilized to evaluate the actual loss and guide the ICNN parameter updates, formulating a simulation-in-the-loop structure and enhancing the practicality of DOE results. A backpropagation algorithm is proposed to derive parameter gradients theoretically, which achieves efficient training and better physical interpretability. Numerical experiments validate the superiority of the proposed E2E-SiL framework, which enhances the practicality of DOE results and ensures better utilization of DERs.

title: Link-Based Distributed Co-Optimization of Power Dispatch and EV Routing in Solar Pavement-Enabled Power-Transportation Networks
abstract: Solar pavements (SPs) can offer clean electricity and accommodate road traffic, thereby enabling coupled power-transportation networks (CPTNs) from the generation side. However, SPs that are inherently dual-functional may introduce conflicts in the CPTN coordination, making the integrated management of SP performance and electric vehicle (EV) routing challenging. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a link-based approach for coordinated scheduling of SP-enabled power-transportation networks. Specifically, we establish a generalized analytical SP generation model considering the actual SP structure and dynamic shadow of vehicles to guarantee the accurate SP generation estimation. Then, we develop a novel link-based mixed user equilibrium model that employs link flows as decision variables, circumventing the complex feasible route generation required by traditional route-based models. Besides, we design a tailored endogenous flow-dependent toll to adaptively and dynamically regulate traffic flows on SP links by integrating SP generation performance and link congestion level. Under mild conditions, we prove that there exists a unique equilibrium solution. To preserve privacy between two entities, a stable and adaptive alternating direction of multipliers method (SA-ADMM) based on the regularized Barzilai-Borwein scheme is developed to efficiently solve the coordinated optimization model. Numerical studies validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Routing and Scheduling of Mobile Energy Storage Systems for Distribution Network Resilience Enhancement Based on a Hybrid Data-Model Driven Approach
abstract: Mobile Energy Storage Systems (MESSs) are critical for improving distribution network resilience under extreme weather events. However, the mathematical model for MESS routing and scheduling is essentially a high-dimensional mixed-integer nonlinear stochastic optimization problem. To accurately and rapidly obtain the routing and scheduling of MESSs and the optimal operation of distribution networks, a bi-level optimization of MESS routing and scheduling based on a hybrid data-model driven approach is proposed. In the upper level, the data-driven approach is achieved by the graph attention network multi-agent conservative soft actor-critic reinforcement learning (GMARL) to determine optimal routing decisions for MESS in the transportation network while taking into account traffic flow and road repair time uncertainties. The proposed GMARL takes full advantage of a graph attention network for feature extraction, and adopts the multi-agent conservative soft actor-critic to mitigate overestimation caused by out-of-distribution experiences, thereby effectively coordinating multiple MESSs to achieve the optimal strategy. In the lower level, a mixed-integer second-order cone programming is formulated to obtain optimal scheduling strategies for MESSs, reconfiguration and optimal power flow in the distribution network. Upon determining the scheduling strategies and amount of load recovery, the reward function value for each MESS can be calculated and used to update the neural network parameters of GMARL, thereby further optimizing the routing strategies of MESSs. Finally, case studies on an IEEE 33-bus active distribution network and a 12-node transportation network are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: Optimal Operation Trajectory Control of Variable Speed Pumped Storage for Power System Frequency Regulation
abstract: Variable speed pumped storage (VSPS) possesses significant potential for power system frequency regulation. This paper proposes a novel optimal trajectory control for VSPS to enhance power system frequency response (FR) by fully leveraging its regulation potential, while maintaining its rotor speed stability. First, the speed stability of VSPS during FR process in both turbine and pump modes is investigated. Following this, an analytical expression for the rotor speed is derived, specifically for the turbine mode, given its susceptibility to speed instability. This expression enables not only an efficient assessment of rotor overspeed risks but also a precise characterization of critical points along the operational trajectory. Then, the design principles of additional power control for VSPS are proposed to achieve a smooth switch of operation stages. Based on these principles and derived expressions, the optimal operation trajectory of VSPS is determined by system disturbances and the unit's operating conditions. This adaptability of the proposed strategy optimizes power response and strengthens FR capability. Furthermore, an overspeed control is developed to ensure rotor speed stability. Finally, the IEEE 39-bus system is utilized to test the proposed strategy under various operating conditions, demonstrating its superior performance in improving power system FR.

title: Coordination Control Strategy of MTDC Connected Offshore Wind Farms Based on Model Predictive Control
abstract: This paper proposes a coordination control strategy (CCS) for voltage source converter (VSC) multi-terminal direct current (MTDC) connected offshore wind farms (WFs) based on model predictive control (MPC). Firstly, to optimize active and reactive power control of WFs, an MPC-based wind turbine (WT) control strategy is designed for fatigue load suppressing and keeping WTs voltage range. Secondly, to optimize the voltage of VSCs, an MPC-based adaptive droop control (ADC) of VSCs is proposed for tracking the WFs power of WF side VSCs (WFVSCs), reducing DC network power loss or achieving power sharing of grid side VSCs (GSVSCs). To formulate MPC optimization problem, the higher-order term with respect to droop coefficient is reduced order and stability of the ADC method is analyzed analysis. Finally, the combined whole system model including multiple WFs, WFVSCs and GSVSCs is used to realize multi-objective optimization. A test system consisted of 3 WFs with 100 × 5 MW WTs, 3 WFVSCs and 2 GSVSCs was used to verify the proposed combined control scheme in MATLAB/Simulink.

title: Multi-objective Non-causal Optimal Control of an Active Pumping System for a Floating Wind Platform
abstract: Semi-submersible floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs) are susceptible to undesirable wave- and wind-induced pitch motion which may be reduced by control strategies. Presently these mainly rely on passive damping, which becomes ineffective under varying sea states. To address this issue, this paper proposes an active pumping strategy for water ballast using multi-objective non-causal optimal controller to suppress pitch motion by pumping water among three columns, thereby generating a counteracting moment against wave and wind excitations. Firstly, the dynamic model of the triple-column VolturnUS floating platform, coupled with hydrodynamic and aerodynamic forces, is developed using the Euler–Lagrange method. Based on this model, a multi-objective non-causal optimal controller is developed to balance pitch motion suppression and pumping power. When pitch minimization is prioritized, compared with the conventional passive damping control, the proposed method reduces the pitch motion by 85% but with high power demand. When power consumption is penalized, the controller can still reduce the pitch by 82% while lowering power usage by 95%, indicating a trade-off between motion suppression and pump energy consumption.

title: Renewable Scenario Generation Using Quantum Generative Adversarial Networks
abstract: With the increasing penetration of renewable resources in modern power systems, scenario generation for renewable energy has emerged as a critical tool for system operation and planning. Among the widely studied methods, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are popular. Despite its model-free nature, it suffers from high computational demands due to its extensive trainable parameters and often struggles to capture intricate data patterns. To address these challenges, we employ quantum computing techniques that harness quantum entanglement principles. We propose, for the first time, a method of generating a quantum-enhanced renewable energy scenario based on a hybrid quantum GANs (QGANs) architecture. Specifically, given historical data of renewable resources, we design a quantum generator using parameterized quantum circuits. This quantum neural network achieves superior expressivity compared to its classical counterparts while requiring significantly fewer trainable parameters. Then, the resulting QGANs architecture combines this quantum generator with a classical discriminator for the effective generation of renewable energy scenarios. Quantum measurements also inherently introduce randomness into the generated renewable scenarios. The simulation results verify the rationale of the proposed method and demonstrate its effectiveness in capturing the spatio-temporal characteristics of renewable resources.
