title: Day-ahead Scheduling of Hydrogen-based Chemical Industry Park: A Bayesian Nonparametric Two-sided Chance Constraint Method
abstract: Uncertainties introduced by renewable energy pose significant challenges to the scheduling of chemical industry parks that integrate an electricity-heat-hydrogen microgrid at the supply level and ammonia-based process chemical industry loads (APCILs) at the demand level. In this paper, a day-ahead scheduling framework based on Bayesian nonparametric two-sided chance constraint (BNTCC) is proposed to address these challenges. First, a refined operation model for electricity-heat-hydrogen microgrids and an integrated energy-material model for APCILs are developed, and the security constraints of hydrogen equipment and chemical production processes are incorporated. Second, a Dirichlet process mixture model (DPMM) is used to construct a Gaussian mixture (GM) distribution from historical uncertainty data to characterize renewable energy uncertainties. On the basis of this GM model, a two-sided chance constraint (TCC) scheduling method is proposed for the scheduling of chemical industry parks to reduce conservatism while ensuring that operational limits are jointly satisfied with a specified confidence level. Finally, to solve the TCC problem efficiently, a second-order cone programming (SOCP) formulation is derived using a piecewise linear (PWL) approximation. An additional algorithm is introduced to accelerate the computation by optimally selecting the PWL segments. Case studies illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for the day-ahead scheduling of chemical industry parks. Compared with state-of-the-art benchmark methods, the proposed method demonstrates superior cost effectiveness and computational efficiency.

title: Prediction-Based Interval Voltage Regulation Involving PV-BESS Coordination
abstract: Modern distribution networks face critical voltage security challenges due to high penetration of photovoltaic (PV) systems and battery energy storage systems (BESSs). Traditional regulation strategies have proven inadequate in mitigating rapid voltage violations caused by power fluctuations. Therefore, a prediction-based proportional coordinated power compensation method is proposed for interval voltage regulation (VR). Firstly, an improved convolutional neural network model is established to predict variable power flows by considering PV and load characteristics, enabling accurate voltage profile prediction. Then, the crucial bus with the most voltage violation is identified, and the optimal coordination ratios for reactive power compensation (RPC) and active power compensation (APC) are determined by an optimization process based on dynamic sensitivity analysis. Furthermore, the crucial bus VR method sequentially allocates RPC from PV inverters and APC from BESSs using a sensitivity-based proportional coordination. Finally, the test results demonstrate an effective VR across all buses over a 24-hour operation, with total RPC and APC requirements reduced by $41.8\%$ and $34.5\%$ in a real 10-bus network, and by $79.1\%$ and $39.5\%$ in the IEEE 123-bus network, respectively.

title: Hierarchical Flexibility Aggregation of Heterogeneous Demand-Side Energy Storages for Secondary Frequency Regulation
abstract: Demand-side energy storages (DESs), such as household batteries and electric vehicles (EVs), have shown great potential in providing fast frequency regulation services. This paper proposes a three-layer hierarchical flexibility aggregation framework to fully evaluate and reliably realize the aggregate flexibility of heterogeneous DESs for secondary frequency regulation (SFR). At the device layer, the regulation capacity of an individual DES is modeled as a two-dimensional feasible region, with the real-time state-of-charge (SoC) constraint and the statistical features of regulation signals well considered. On this basis, heterogeneous DESs are divided into several clusters according to the geometry of their feasible region. At the cluster layer, regulation capacity, dynamic response model as well as regulation costs are efficiently aggregated within each DES cluster by prototype-based maximum inner approximation (MIA). At the aggregator layer, an analytical expression of the multi-cluster coordinated SFR flexibility can be formulated by convex optimizations at each feasible operating point, which provides a comprehensive model for DES aggregators to economically participate in SFR. Comparative simulations validate that the proposed method can accurately capture the aggregate SFR flexibility of heterogeneous DESs with lower flexibility loss and affordable computational burden, while the disaggregation feasibility of aggregate flexibility is further demonstrated using real-world regulation signals.

title: Unified Transmission-Distribution Coordination for Secure and Economical Frequency Support From Distributed Energy Resources
abstract: Utilizing numerous distributed energy resources (DERs) for frequency regulation is a promising pathway to enhance the security and economy of future power systems. However, a fundamental challenge arises from the emergent collective behavior of these resources: their aggregated response, intended to support macro-level system frequency, can jeopardize micro-level local voltage security within distribution networks. To this end, this paper proposes a unified hierarchical framework based on the principle of synergistic co-design. The framework employs a stage-dependent architecture that systematically integrates distinct control strategies for different regulation stages. For security-critical response, it utilizes a novel stage-aware adaptive virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control method with stability formally proven by Lyapunov analysis, while for economic efficiency, it transitions to a distributed control method for cost-optimal restoration. The entire process is underpinned by a proactive voltage security management strategy that enforces micro-level safety. To enable efficient analysis of these complex dynamics, a dual time-scale information interaction mechanism is designed to accelerate the transmission-distribution (T&D) co-simulation process. Simulations on a hybrid transmission-distribution test system validate the framework's effectiveness, demonstrating that the proposed approach enables scalable, secure, and economical frequency support while effectively managing the emergent voltage challenges from collective DER control.

title: Uniformity Analysis of Frequency Regulation for Grid-Following and Grid-Forming Wind Turbines and Distributed Cooperative Frequency Control for Hybrid Wind Farms
abstract: Large numbers of grid-connected wind farms challenge frequency stability. Hybrid wind farms (HWFs) with both grid-following (GFL) and grid-forming (GFM) wind turbines (WTs) are better adapted to wide-ranging changes in grid state. However, the frequency support capability of each wind turbine in an HWF depends on factors like wind speed and control type. Current controls do not fully exploit the grid frequency support potential of each WT in different states. Hence, this paper first analyzes the frequency regulation characteristics of GFL WTs and virtual synchronous generator (VSG)-based GFM WTs, revealing the uniformity between them. Furthermore, a distributed cooperative frequency control (DCFC) for HWFs is proposed to improve grid frequency stability. DCFC uses a leaderless consistency algorithm to allocate the output active power of each wind turbine according to the state of the different WTs. Additionally, the adaptive optimisation feature of DCFC adjusts the frequency support coefficients of the wind turbines in real time as their rotor kinetic energy varies, improving the safety of the WTs. Finally, the GFL and GFM frequency regulation uniformity theory and the DCFC are comprehensively verified. The results show that DCFC improves the security of the WTs and enhances the frequency support capability compared to centralised control.

title: Aggregated Distributed Photovoltaics-Based Active Fast Power-Frequency Regulation in the New Power System
abstract: The large-scale integration of distributed photovoltaics (PVs) in the new power system increases the proportion of dispatchable resources, enabling their participation in fast power-frequency regulation (FPFR) of the system. However, the large number and wide distribution of distributed PVs limit their ability to directly participate in regulation. To address this issue, this paper proposes a hierarchical fast power-frequency regulation method based on aggregated distributed PVs. Firstly, to tackle the aggregation difficulty posed by the diverse locations, capacities, and adjustment capabilities of distributed PVs, a clustering-based aggregation method for distributed PVs is proposed, which utilizes the multi-dimensional characteristics of distributed PVs to precisely quantify the node relationships and then optimize the modularity function, thereby achieving the accurate aggregation of distributed PVs. Secondly, to mitigate the impact of power fluctuations and nonlinearity in aggregated distributed PVs on their participation in second-timescale FPFR, a combined prediction method is proposed, which integrates the strengths of both Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model and grey system model to enable faster and more accurate power prediction of the aggregated distributed PVs in the next few seconds. Furthermore, considering the effect of information and electricity flow among aggregations, a consensus-based power allocation strategy is designed from a cyber-physical fusion perspective. This strategy dynamically adjusts communication paths to mitigate the impact of communication delays while simultaneously minimizing the line power losses among aggregations. Finally, simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Preference-Oriented Evolutionary Multi-Objective Energy-Noise Optimization for Fast Wind Farm Layout Design
abstract: Mitigating wind farm noise through layout optimiza-tion while maintaining power production under varying noise limits remains challenging. To reduce workload and decision time, and engage DMs more in optimization, this study pro-poses a preference-oriented evolutionary multi-objective (EMO) framework for wind farm layout optimization that incorporates decision-makers' (DMs') preferences through interactively up-dated reference points. The framework guides the search toward DMs' regions of interest effectively while preserving population diversity. Case studies on a real-world wind farm show that the proposed algorithm outperforms four state-of-the-art EMO algorithms and a traditional layout method. Compared with the real-world layouts, the resulting solutions reduce the noise level by 10.45%-23.04% and increase the annual energy production by 3.03%-4.09%, while aligning with DMs' preferences.

title: Dual-Time-Scale Dynamic Active Wake Control Using Stochastic Yaw Optimization and Distributed Axial Induction Optimization for Large-Scale Wind Farm
abstract: As the scale of wind farms (WFs) and the number of wind turbines (WTs) continue to increase, the calculation efficiency of centralized active wake control (AWC) methods can not satisfy the real-time performance requirement. To address this issue, a dual-time-scale dynamic AWC strategy for large-scale WF is proposed in this paper. First, a centralized AWC model is developed which incorporates a dual-time-scale control strategy. The optimal yaw angle is obtained by long-term scale stochastic optimization under the time-varying wind conditions to maximize the power generation potential of WF, and different WF operating modes can be achieved by short-term scale dynamic axial induction control. Then, a spectral clustering-based WF partitioning method is introduced. The wake coupling can be obtained by engineering wake model, and the WF can be divided into multiple subregions through efficient matrix computations and eigenvalue analysis. Finally, in order to improve the calculation speed, the centralized AWC optimization problem is decomposed into several smaller subproblems that can be solved in a distributed manner based on the partitioning results. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method obtains reasonable WF partitioning, owns excellent power generation and fatigue load suppression performance under time-varying wind conditions, and significantly improves calculation speed.

title: Optimal Planning for Offshore Wind Farm Electrical Collector System Considering $N-1$ Criterion
abstract: With the rise of renewable energy-centered power systems, offshore wind has emerged as a cornerstone of the clean energy transition. Despite the growing demand for highly reliable and cost-effective electrical collector system (ECS) planning, existing research based on the $N-1$ security criterion remains largely confined to conventional single-/double-sided ring topologies and heuristic algorithms, thus falling short in balancing the tradeoff between economic performance and stringent reliability requirements. In this paper, we propose a novel ECS planning framework for offshore wind farms (OWFs) by developing a scenario-based $N-1$ composite ring planning model. Furthermore, the proposed framework is extended to support cable size selection through mathematical optimization models for both double-sided ring topology and $N-1$ composite ring topology. To reduce computational complexity, model simplification and acceleration strategies are adopted. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior optimization outcomes under the $N-1$ framework compared with conventional methods.

title: Stability Assessment and Impact Analysis on LCC-HVDC System Considering the Dynamic Characteristic of Receiving-Side Converter
abstract: With the increasing installed capacity of wind power, the line-commutated converter-based high-voltage direct-current (LCC-HVDC) in sending AC grid encounters potential issues of sub/super-synchronous oscillations (SSSOs), posing a threat to the stable operation of power system. The impedance-based approach has proven to be a useful tool for investigating SSSOs in power electronic device-based systems, relying on the accurate impedance model. However, most existing studies on the stability of LCC-HVDC system simplify the receiving-side converter to an ideal DC voltage source, which ignores the AC-DC dynamics of the receiving-side converter and grid, causing inaccuracy in stability assessment. Moreover, there is a lack of clarity regarding the effect of the receiving-side system on oscillation stability. Thus, this paper establishes the complete impedance model of the LCC-HVDC considering the receiving-side system, by proposing a unified small signal transfer path framework for the LCC converter. Subsequently, the stability of the complete LCC-HVDC system is assessed, and the effect of the receiving-side system on the oscillation characteristics of SSSOs is investigated based on the DC impedance network in detail. Finally, a second-order quantitative index is defined to evaluate the influence factors on the receiving-side interaction, and the conditions for neglecting this interaction are discussed.

title: Seamless Grid-Connected/Islanded Transition in Fully Grid-Forming PV Powered Microgrids
abstract: This paper investigates the full-state virtual oscillator control (fVOC) method to realize the flexible operation of 100% PV-powered microgrid. In the grid-connected mode, the enhanced DC voltage stability of fVOC enables the grid-forming PVs to provide the dynamic support while being compatible with the maximum power point tracking function. This dual capability is critical to replace the grid-following operation under the very high penetration of renewable sources. In the islanded situation, the reconnection of the microgrid to the bulk grid leads to large phase jumps, which can trigger the overcurrent saturation and induce the DC voltage instability in grid-forming PVs. To address this issue, a phase adaption current limiting method in fVOC is proposed. The full-order system modeling is performed to guide the parameter design of the proposed method. The Lyapunov function is derived to reveal the enhanced transient stability of the grid-forming PV system during the reconnection of the islanded microgrid. The superiority of the proposed method is verified in both simulations and field tests in a 100% PV powered microgrid. The mode transition between grid-connected and islanded is seamless without islanding detection and pre-synchronization.

title: Analytical Evaluation of Voltage Stability Based on Stability Region Boundary and Probability Transformation Method
abstract: An analytical method for probabilistic voltage stability evaluation is proposed, which integrates the voltage stability region boundary (VSRB) and probability transformation method (PTM) while accounting for the uncertainty impact of renewable energy. A second-order polynomial is employed to approximate the VSRB, balancing efficiency and accuracy when applied to large-scale power grids. Through the VSRB, the voltage instability probability is formulated as a function of random variables and control variables; the PTM is then utilized to derive the analytical expression of this function, which is designated as the probabilistic voltage stability region boundary (PVSRB) in this paper. Leveraging the PVSRB, the global voltage stability state of the system can be comprehensively grasped, and the voltage instability probability at any operating point (OP) can be rapidly obtained. Testing on an improved New England 39-bus system and an improved 1888-bus system, results from the proposed method are compared against those from Monte Carlo simulation (MCS), cumulant method (CM), and the polynomial chaos expansion method (PCEM). The proposed method has shown good performance in both accuracy and efficiency.

title: Frequency-Sharing Scheme for IPC-CSC Offshore Wind MTDC Systems Using Logistic Function
abstract: The current source converter-based multi-terminal DC (CSC-MTDC) system with improved phase control (IPC) method provides a promising solution for transmitting offshore wind power to multiple AC grids. However, the AC voltage control mechanism of such systems has not been fully investigated, and the inherent DC decoupling characteristics make it difficult to suppress frequency disturbances caused by wind speed fluctuations. To address these issues, this paper establishes the mathematical model of the IPC-CSC and proposes an offshore AC voltage control strategy by constructing intermediate variables, thereby ensuring the stable operation of the overall system. Furthermore, a frequency-sharing coordinated control strategy is proposed, where independent power and frequency control loops and voltage compensation are introduced. Thus, multiple receiving AC systems can jointly share power disturbances and fully utilize frequency regulation resources. In addition, an adaptive droop control method based on a logistic function is designed to provide smooth and bounded frequency support under different levels of frequency deviation. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategies is validated through simulation and hardware-in-the-loop experiment results.

title: An Energy Diverting Converter Topology for AC Fault Ride-Through in Series-Connected Offshore Wind Power System
abstract: In series-connected offshore wind power system (SC-OWPS), wind turbines are connected in series to obtain high voltage direct current (HVDC) for power transmission. This configuration eliminates the need for huge offshore platforms, significantly reducing costs and losses. In SC-OWPS, with full-bridge modular multilevel converter (FB-MMC) being the onshore converter and controlling the DC link current, DC voltages of FB-MMC and wind turbines vary from zero to the nominal value. During severe onshore AC faults, existing parallel-connected energy diverting converters (PC-EDCs) are unable to meet the power dissipation requirement in a low DC link voltage. To address this issue, a novel series-connected EDC (SC-EDC) suitable for SC-OWPS is presented in this paper. During AC faults, a new feedback control for FB-MMC’s overall capacitor voltage is proposed to increase the output voltage of SC-EDC, while FB-MMC reduces its DC link voltage to keep the DC link current unchanged. The proposed SC-EDC features two branches: a main load branch composed of a diode valve and an ultra-fast mechanical switch, and an energy diverting branch comprising cascaded half-bridge and full-bridge energy diverting submodules. The operational principles and control methods of SC-EDC are thoroughly investigated. Finally, the effectiveness of the AC fault ride-through (FRT) strategy and the feasibility of SC-EDC are validated by PSCAD/EMTDC simulation and physical experiment.

title: Transient Stability Analysis of MMC-HVDC Connected DFIG-Based Wind Farms in the Electromechanical Timescale
abstract: This paper investigates the transient stability of doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG)-based wind farms connected via a modular multilevel converter (MMC)-based high-voltage direct-current (HVDC) transmission system in the electromechanical timescale. During faults, the MMC tends to be switched to the current-limiting mode, which further interacts with the control systems of DFIG-based wind farms, thereby complicating the transient stability problem. In this paper, a large-signal model is constructed for transient stability analysis under this condition. The transient stability mechanism is revealed, and a transient stability index that considers the impact of a phase-locked loop in the electromechanical timescale is derived. The proposed index quantitatively assesses the instability risk arising from the coupled interaction between the DFIG-based wind farms and the MMC. In addition, the impacts of the current- limiting mode and other parameters (i.e., speed control loop gains, rotor shaft damping, inertia coefficient and fault location and severity) are analyzed. Based on the results of the parametric analysis, a suite of targeted countermeasures is proposed to enhance the transient stability of the power system. Finally, a theoretical analysis is demonstrated and verified through hardware-in-the-loop simulations using the Modeling Tech microgrid real-time simulation platform.

title: Assessment of the Steady-State Security Region for Integrated Medium-Voltage and Low-Voltage Active Distribution Networks
abstract: The security region (SR) of a distribution network (DN) is typically characterized as a connected set consisting of nodal active and reactive power injections that ensure the operational security of the DN, and is an important security metric. With extensive integration of distributed photovoltaic systems into low-voltage (LV) DNs, recent studies advocate that medium-voltage (MV) DN security assessment should entail LV security constraints. However, assessing the SR for an integrated MV and LV (IMLV) DN is concerned little in prior studies and is a challenging task at both modeling and solution levels. Firstly, to address the issue of inaccuracies in LV DN models, a pre-designed outlier-immune two-sided conservative linear approximation method is proposed to recover the LV DN model with satisfactory accuracy for the subsequent assessment. Then, an SR assessment model based on two-stage robust optimization is proposed that incorporates the constraints related to network equipment and uncertainties. To reduce computational time, a feasible inexact column-and-constraint generation (FI-C&CG) algorithm is further designed. Case studies on different scales of multi-phase DNs demonstrate the necessity of considering the interaction between the MV and LV DNs when assessing the SR, and showcase the superior computational performance of the FI-C&CG algorithm compared to the regular C&CG.

title: A Fault-Tolerant Power Processing Architecture for Resilient LVDC Networks with Integrated Photovoltaics
abstract: This paper proposes a novel fault-tolerant power processing architecture for photovoltaic (PV) systems within low-voltage direct current (LVDC) networks, aimed at enhancing operational resilience and reliability in sustainable energy systems. The architecture integrates a bidirectional dc/dc converter for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) and a buck converter to supply a stable 24 V output from a 48 V LVDC bus, ensuring seamless operation for distributed consumer loads under varying environmental and fault conditions. Fault-tolerance is achieved through built-in redundancy and adaptive control mechanisms that support continuous operation during converter failures. The proposed system's performance is evaluated through comprehensive case studies and real-time hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing using the OPAL-RT platform. Results demonstrate the system's effectiveness in maintaining energy continuity and voltage stability, highlighting its potential for deployment in resilient, PV-integrated LVDC networks supporting sustainable energy goals.

title: Stability Region Analysis for HVDC-Connected Off-shore Wind Farm Participating in Grid Frequency Support
abstract: When the high-voltage direct current-connected offshore wind farm (HVDC-connected OWF) participates in grid frequency support, excessively high frequency controller gains may exacerbate the electromagnetic oscillations within system. Therefore, it is essential to study the stability region for frequency controller gains of HVDC-connected OWF, thus ensuring the grid secure operation during frequency events. Currently, numerical methods are used to analyze the operational stability region of HVDC-connected OWF. However, these methods involve exhaustive calculations to obtain the stability region, resulting in a significant computational burden. To address the issue, this work proposes an analytical stability region identification method for HVDC-connected OWF when it participates in the grid frequency support. Specifically, a comprehensive small signal model, tailored for analyzing frequency support-induced oscillation, is first developed by considering both the frequency regulation characteristics and the power converter dynamics. Further, using the Padé approximation technique, the reduced order equivalent model is derived while preserving its accuracy. With this equivalent model, the mechanism underlying frequency support-induced oscillation is qualitatively elucidated, and the stability region for frequency support is also analytically derived. Finally, the analysis results are validated through electromagnetic transient simulations.

title: Reconfiguration-Driven Flexibility Extensions in Coupled Power-Transportation Networks With Uncertainties
abstract: Under high photovoltaic (PV) penetration, distribution networks (DNs) face insufficient operational flexibility across both spatial and temporal dimensions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a reconfiguration-driven framework aimed at flexibility extensions for coupled power-transportation networks under uncertainty, which seeks to improve the operational flexibility of DNs. The framework leverages multi-reconfiguration-driven spatiotemporally controllable devices to enable multi-level reconfiguration of feeders, voltage source converters and modular transportable energy storage systems, thereby facilitating cross-node and cross-period energy coordination while significantly enhancing scheduling flexibility and PV utilization efficiency. To handle uncertainties from traffic congestion, load fluctuations, and PV generation, a dynamic-distance-based spatiotemporal decision-making method integrated with rolling optimization is developed to represent the time-varying spatial relationships of vehicles and battery modules during transportation and scheduling, while addressing future uncertainties and enhancing the adaptability of the scheduling strategy. Furthermore, modular battery availability screening and safety assurance model are incorporated to support dynamic identification and refined management of battery modules, preventing over-charging/over-discharging and state mismatches. Simulation studies on both a modified IEEE 33-node distribution network with a 14-node transportation network and a 10 kV, 220-node distribution network in a specific region of Anhui Province, China demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively extends DN flexibility, enhances PV utilization, and ensures reliable operation.

title: A Nonlinear Drivetrain Torsional Oscillation Damper for WTGs: Robust Rejection of Large Disturbances With Balanced Noise Immunity
abstract: Drivetrain torsional oscillations in wind turbine generators (WTGs) challenge power system reliability and stability due to nonlinearities and uncertainties, especially under large disturbances, while measurement noise further degrades damper performance. This paper develops a nonlinear drivetrain torsional oscillation damper (DTOD) within an active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) framework. To adapt to its standard form, the nonlinear drivetrain dynamics of grid-connected WTG are exactly transformed into a second-order Brunovsky canonical form using differential homeomorphism coordinate transformation. DTOD parameters, including those of the extended state observer (ESO) and nonlinear state error feedback (NLSEF), are Pareto-optimally tuned through normalized multi-objective frequency-domain optimization, enhancing the robust rejection of large disturbance while balancing the trade-off with noise immunity. The fully decentralized DTOD relies only on local measurements, supporting scalable deployment across large wind farms. Simulation results under various large disturbance scenarios in grid-connected single and multiple wind farms validate the effectiveness, advantages, robustness, and scalability of the proposed nonlinear WTG DTOD.

title: Coordinated Interaction Between EV Charging Stations and Distribution Network via Stepwise Droop Control with SoC Interval Management
abstract: The flexible charging capability of electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) can improve distribution network (DN) operation with source-load uncertainties. To fully harness this potential, this paper proposes a three-stage coordinated interaction method between EVCSs and the DN, centered on a novel stepwise droop control function. In the first stage, a dynamic state of charge (SoC) interval management approach is introduced to determine the optimal SoC interval and the corresponding adjustable power interval for EVCSs, considering charging uncertainties and temporal coupling of energy. The second stage is implemented from the DN perspective using grid-wide information to optimize P-V stepwise droop control functions for EVCSs. To alleviate the computational burden from binary variables, a general binary reduction technique is adopted. In the last stage, each EVCS decomposes the obtained stepwise droop control function into multiple levels of charging power for individual EVs, considering the minimal changes in charging power and the satisfaction of target SoC. Consequently, in real time, the EVCS can self-regulate the charging power based on local voltage measurements. The simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed interaction method. Compared with the baseline method, it reduces the DN's average voltage deviation and power loss by 13.29% and 14.68%, respectively.

title: Low-Carbon Scheduling for Power-Hydrogen Integrated Energy System Using Large Language Model Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Power-hydrogen integrated energy systems (PH-IESs) are emerging as a promising solution to achieve net-zero carbon emissions. However, the large-scale integration of uncertain renewable energy sources (RESs) and flexible demand-side resources (e.g., hydrogen electrolysis) pose great challenges in the real-time low-carbon scheduling of PH-IESs. This paper proposes a novel source-demand coordinated low-carbon scheduling framework for PH-IESs, empowered by deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and large language model (LLM) techniques. The proposed framework systematically integrates source-side generation with demand-side flexible hydrogen loads to improve carbon reduction and economic efficiency. An LLM-enhanced carbon flow pattern recognition and inference mechanism is developed to enable accurate predictions of real-time carbon intensity under complex, high-dimensional operating conditions. An LLM-enhanced DRL algorithm is then proposed to directly generate optimal scheduling strategies for the flexible demand-side resources, which can overcome computational bottlenecks in real-time decision-making. Numerical simulations on two PH-IESs are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating DRL and LLM techniques for intelligent, efficient, and low-carbon operation of PH-IESs.

title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Flexible Control in MTDC System for Offshore Wind Farm Integration
abstract: Converter power sharing and DC voltage regulation are critical control objectives in voltage source converter-based multi-terminal high-voltage DC (VSC-MTDC) systems, particularly when incorporating massive offshore wind farms (OWFs). However, the inherent variability and intermittency of OWFs pose significant challenges to conventional model-based and optimization-based control methods, which often rely on accurate system modeling and extensive computation. Moreover, traditional heuristic optimization approaches are prone to local optima, limiting their ability to handle rapidly fluctuating wind power conditions effectively. Reinforcement Learning (RL), with its capability to adaptively optimize control policies through continuous interaction with dynamic environments, presents a promising alternative. This paper proposes a novel RL-based control strategy for DC voltage regulation and proportional power sharing, leveraging an adaptive droop control mechanism. The Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm is employed to dynamically adjust local droop coefficients, benefiting from its robustness in continuous action spaces and its ability to mitigate the effects of OWF power fluctuations. To enhance optimization efficiency and accelerate convergence, a combined MTDC system pre-evaluation and PPO initialization method is introduced. The proposed RL-based control strategy is validated through dynamic simulations of a five-terminal MTDC grid in MATLAB/Simulink, demonstrating superior performance in handling various disturbances and contingencies associated with OWF integration.

title: End-to-End Collaborative Optimization for Active Distribution Network Power Dispatch Based on Sparse Model-Ensemble Learning Policy
abstract: With the higher penetration of distributed renewable power sources, novel active distribution networks are increasingly implementing flexible adjustment strategies. Currently, the dual uncertainties from both sources and demand significantly affect power dispatch in distribution networks. Typically, power dispatch is performed using a predict-then-optimize approach, making it challenging to quantify the gap between the real-time and theoretically optimal dispatch performances due to inaccuracies in power predictions. Hence, this study introduces a novel end-to-end policy to solve a collaborative optimization between prediction and dispatch. The policy directly utilizes all available information, such as gridded numerical weather forecasts, for dispatch decision-making, which eliminates the need for power predictions as intermediate variables for dispatch. To address the challenges of high-dimensional and open-scenario model training in end-to-end policies, sparse model-ensemble learning is proposed to formulate the dispatch policy model. The model is solved using constrained policy optimization. Comparative studies show that the proposed end-to-end policy outperforms the predict-then-optimize policy in real-time dispatch cases involving photovoltaic reactive power ancillary service and demand response within distribution networks.

title: Adaptive Perceptual Graph Learning for Robust Wind Power Forecasting Under Incomplete Observations
abstract: Reliable wind power forecasting plays a crucial role in enabling efficient scheduling and effective energy management in virtual power plants. However, incomplete data observations caused by sensor malfunctions and volatile environmental conditions significantly compromise the reliability of wind power forecasting. To address these challenges, this paper presents a robust adaptive perceptual graph learning framework designed to enhance forecasting accuracy and robustness. The proposed framework uses an attention-gated GRU encoder to restore spatiotemporal dependencies under incomplete observations and integrates an adaptive graph convolution module to dynamically capture complex, non-stationary spatial correlations between wind turbines. To further promote physical consistency, a physics-informed discriminator is introduced as a plug-in component, guiding the model to align its outputs with the nonlinear aerodynamic relationship between wind speed and power generation. In addition, a sensitivity-aware adjustment strategy is developed to dynamically emphasize low-speed operating regimes. Comprehensive experiments conducted on real-world wind farm datasets show that the proposed method consistently surpasses baseline approaches, achieving a reduction of up to 35% in mean absolute percentage error, even under severe missing data scenarios.

title: Distributed Control of Multi-Voltage-Level DC Microgrids for Resilient Renewable Interconnection
abstract: The dc microgrid (MG) has become an effective platform for integrating renewable energy sources (RESs) and energy storage systems, particularly in standalone configurations where local generation and loads are clustered. To enable complementary utilization of RESs across multiple islanded dc MGs, the triple active bridge converter (TABC) offers an attractive solution for interconnecting dc MGs with different voltage levels. This paper develops a distributed and resilient multi-port coordinated control strategy for TABC-interlinked dc MGs, enabling unified power regulation and fault-tolerant operation. The proposed method adapts seamlessly to various operating modes: it enables proportional power sharing among interconnected dc MGs under normal conditions, and it maintains uninterrupted power coordination through a consistent control scheme under fault conditions. This strategy enhances system resilience by ensuring continuous operation unaffected by faults while avoiding controller disturbances. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through hardware-in-the-loop experiments on a Typhoon-HIL platform.

title: Coordinated Optimization of Coupled Power–Traffic Networks: A Hierarchical SUE Method Considering Behavioral Preferences and Uncertainty
abstract: The rapid proliferation of electric vehicles intensifies the interdependence between transportation and power networks, posing operational challenges due to stochastic routing decisions and the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of charging demand. This paper proposes a hybrid decision-making framework that integrates user behavioral modeling with system-level optimization for coupled power-traffic networks. First, we develop network models that incorporate integrated energy stations (ESs) and heterogeneous vehicle classifications grouped by charging requirements and grid-response capabilities. Second, we formulate a hierarchical nested logit-based stochastic user equilibrium model to characterize multi-level user decisions under uncertainty. Furthermore, a collaborative power-traffic dispatch model is constructed to minimize generalized user costs, encompassing travel, charging, ES attributes, and power distribution network operation. A two-stage distributed solution algorithm is further developed to ensure computational tractability. Case studies on two test systems demonstrate the method's efficacy in characterizing user behavioral uncertainties and coordinating integrated power-traffic flows.

title: LPV Model Predictive Control for Offshore Wind Farms Considering Wake Delay Characteristics
abstract: The pronounced wake effect in large-scale offshore wind farm necessitates careful consideration of its delay characteristics, which are crucial yet often overlooked in control. Addressing the coupling between the dynamic evolution of wake effects and the parameter changes of the WT control model, this paper introduces a Linear Parameter-Varying (LPV) model predictive control method that considers wake delay characteristics. Through the development of a quasi-steady state wake model, the wake delay characteristic is incorporated within an LPV model for the wind farm. A two-stage dimensionality reduction method is proposed to simplify the calculation, and a model predictive control (MPC) method is combined to optimize the fatigue damage balance and power generation enhancement in the wind farm coordinately. Simulation results from a wind farm consisting of 16 wind turbines validate the efficacy of the quasi-steady state wake model in depicting the spatial distribution of wake delays. Furthermore, in dynamically varying wind speed and directions scenarios, the proposed control method can effectively capture the wind speed delay and fluctuation characteristics between different wind turbines, leading to heightening power output and diminishing fatigue stresses. Notably, in comparison to the static model control, the adaptive parameter tuning mechanism inherent in the proposed method effectively curtails control overshoot, enhancing overall system performance.

title: A Novel Learning-Based Optimal Control Strategy for SOFCs in DC Microgrids Using the Recurrent Equilibrium Network
abstract: This paper presents a feedback recurrent equilibrium network (REN)-based linear quadratic regulator for enhancing the control performance of solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) in DC microgrids. The REN is trained offline to approximate unmodeled system dynamics and compensate for disturbances, enabling efficient real-time implementation. The proposed method requires no more than 20 $\mu s$ computational time per control cycle and achieves high control accuracy, with the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) not exceeding 0.2% in stack voltage regulation. The control stability is rigorously proven. Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experiments further demonstrate the practical applicability and superior performance of the proposed controller compared with various methods.

title: Decoupled Controllable-Boundary Model and Coordinated Voltage Support for Renewable Power Plants with Multiple IBRs Under Asymmetric LVRT
abstract: Large-scale renewable power plants (RPPs) should coordinate numerous differentiated inverter-based resources (IBRs) to provide reliable voltage support under low-voltage ride-through (LVRT). Yet the reactive-power controllable boundary (RCB) of multiple IBRs under asymmetric LVRT remains insufficiently explored, limiting support capability and risking local over-voltage. This study develops a unified RCB model that considers the impacts of interactive coupling, phase-locking deviation, and voltage propagation. Then, four tight constraints are derived from RCB vector trajectories on the complex domain plane to shrink the original RCB equations, yielding a linear and decoupled minimum RCB intersection under various fault conditions. The minimum RCB can regulate the conservative distribution of sequence voltage boundaries allowed for each bus based on the RPP's pre-event state. During LVRT, a coordinated voltage support strategy is proposed to distributed adjust reactive outputs of multiple IBRs following an optimal trajectory in the pre-given RCB, which maximizes voltage support capability. The hardware-in-the-loop experiment referred to an actual large-scale RPP project shows that the proposed strategy eliminates local over-voltage risks observed in existing strategies (up to 17.3%) and improves the faulted-phase voltage support capability by 17.48% on average across various fault conditions.

title: Multi-Rate Fast Frequency Regulation With High-Fidelity Neural Network Model of the Electrolyzer Process
abstract: Frequency regulation is crucial for grid stability, especially with the increasing penetration of inverter-based resources (IBRs). Hydrogen electrolyzers, as flexible loads, offer a promising solution by dynamically adjusting power consumption to counteract frequency deviations. While existing studies primarily focus on electrolyzer stacks and power converters, the role of auxiliary process components such as pumps and coolers remains largely unexplored. This paper proposes a multi-rate frequency response (MRFR) model for hydrogen electrolyzer process plants, distinguishing frequency regulation contributions from both the electrolyzer stack and auxiliary components. A high-fidelity neural network (HiFiNN) model is developed using a detailed alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) process model in Aspen HYSYS, accurately capturing the interactions between electrical and thermodynamic parameters. The HiFiNN model is integrated with a model predictive controller (MPC) to optimize frequency regulation while maintaining process stability. The proposed framework is validated through simulations and real-time controller-hardware-in-the-loop (CHIL) experiment to validate its feasibility for practical deployment. Additionally, its effectiveness is demonstrated under varying IBR penetration levels, highlighting its capability to maintain frequency stability in low-inertia power systems.

title: Hybrid-Arm-Based DC Station for Wind Power Collection and HVDC Transmission: Implementation and Operation Supporting Startup
abstract: The startup issue has become a major concern of the offshore wind power collection and transmission system (OWPCTS). To tackle with it, a novel design of offshore station is proposed in this paper with an asymmetrical forward-and-reverse power transmission capability. With the modular multilevel cells and diode units integrating in different phases of bridge arm, the detailed topology of the proposed offshore station is implemented by a special hybrid-arm structure which contributes to smaller footprint and saved cost. During the normal operation mode, the proposed offshore station performs the function of voltage boosting and wind power delivering from wind farm (WF) to onshore station. During the system startup mode, the proposed offshore station reversely transfers the startup power from the onshore station to WF. The corresponding control scheme is presented with the capability of supporting startup. Both simulation and hardware-in-the-loop(HIL) experiment are carried out, and the working performances of the proposed offshore station are validated for typical scenarios.

title: Analytical Analysis of Small-Disturbance Synchronization Stability of 2-VSG System and Stability Enhancement Strategy
abstract: Virtual synchronous generator (VSG) introduces small-disturbance synchronization stability issues similar to synchronous generators. However, most existing research either relies on numerical analysis or focuses on particular operation scenarios, whose conclusions may not be generally applicable. Analytical analysis is the way to address this issue. This paper presents an analytical analysis of small-disturbance synchronization stability in a 2-VSG system considering various operation scenarios. First, the simplified model of the 2-VSG system is built and linearized. Its eigenvalues are analytically approximated, and the accuracy is verified. Then, two sufficient conditions for system stability from the perspective of operation scenarios and control parameters are derived. Hopf bifurcation and transcritical bifurcation are found, and their mechanisms and bifurcation conditions are analyzed. Further, it is proven that the uniform distribution of damping and inertia assists in avoiding bifurcations and ensures system stability under various operation scenarios. The inverse distribution strategy can be applied to improve the damping ratio of low-frequency oscillations only in systems where all VSGs supply power relatively uniformly. Case studies are provided to validate these conclusions. In summary, this paper provides a new perspective on the synchronization stability of the 2-VSG system and an optimistic damping distribution approach to enhance stability.

title: An Enhanced Grid-Forming Control Strategy for DC-Coupled Alkaline Water Electrolyzers
abstract: Recent years have seen the research on the participation of Alkaline water electrolyzers (AWEs) in power grid regulation gained significant traction. In particular, the participation of AWEs in grid-forming (GFM) services is precisely an urgent research topic at present. However, regarding the involvement of AWEs in GFM services, existing studies are typically limited to single AWE units or rely on communication for controlling multiple AWEs. Nor have they considered the capacity variation characteristics of AWEs. Furthermore, the unique topologies of DC-coupled AWE systems require special consideration. To address these issues, this paper proposes an enhanced GFM control strategy for DC-coupled AWE systems. Specifically, the proposed control scheme includes two key improvements. First, a temperature-driven droop control is employed to enable coordinated operation among individual AWE units. Second, an improved DC-link voltage synchronized control (IDVSC) is proposed for the voltage source converter (VSC). Furthermore, the proposed strategy is fully decentralized, allowing both AWE units and the VSC to provide GFM services. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed strategy is validated through simulation and experimental results.

title: Energy Management for Island Electro-Hydrogen Microgrid via Physically-Bounded Distributionally Robust Chance-Constrained Approach
abstract: Island electro-hydrogen microgrid with offshore wind power generation is a promising way to promote the development of marine economy. Data-driven distributionally robust chance-constrained (DRCC) offers a risk-aware framework when the distribution of uncertainties is unknown. However, the general reformulation for DRCC may result in a sub-optimal or an over-conservative solution. This paper focuses on the coordinated energy management of island electro-hydrogen microgrid. First, a comprehensive hydrogen-related model is proposed that incorporates dynamic offshore hydrogen production, storage, and usage, where the multiphysics-aware offshore hydrogen production model for alkaline water electrolysis is introduced. Then, a physically-bounded DRCC model is developed to account for the uncertainty of offshore wind power. An improved metric-based ambiguity set is introduced by enforcing physical bounds on the uncertainty while preserving the exactness, resulting in a bilinear programming problem. Finally, an iterative sequential convex optimization algorithm is tailored to solve the resulting physically-bounded DRCC model with the exact bilinear form and reduce the solution conservatism. Numerical results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: Quantitative Parameter Conditions for Stability and Coupling in GFM–GFL Converter Hybrid Systems From a Small-Signal Synchronous Perspective
abstract: With the development of renewable energy sources, power systems are gradually evolving into a system comprising both grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) converters. However, the dynamic interactions between the two types of converters remain unclear, particularly in the presence of low-inertia GFM converters, due to the fundamental differences in their synchronization mechanisms. To address this gap, this paper develops a small-signal synchronous stability model for power systems containing GFM and GFL converters, which considers network line dynamics. Based on matrix perturbation, we reveal that GFM and GFL subsystems can be effectively decoupled when GFL converters operate near unity power factor or when GFM converters possess sufficiently large inertia or damping, and provide lower bound of control parameters ensuring decoupling. Under the decoupling condition, we propose decentralized and analytical parameter-based stability criteria which have clear physical interpretations: the positive damping of converters compensates for the negative damping of the network. In the case of coupling, we also propose decentralized stability criteria based on the small phase theorem. The effectiveness of the theoretical analysis is validated through simulations in MATLAB/Simulink.

title: A Quantum-Assisted Boltzmann Machine for Wind Power Probabilistic Learning
abstract: Accurate probabilistic modeling of renewable power is essential for the secure operation and control of modern power systems. However, learning and modeling the data structure with high accuracy remains challenging due to the inherent spatial-temporal correlations of renewables. To address this issue, we propose a novel quantum-assisted Gaussian-Bernoulli restricted Boltzmann machine (GBRBM), which is intrinsically suitable for continuous wind power modeling. Furthermore, we tailor its negative phase to be directly solvable by quantum computing, thereby accelerating the learning process. Experiments conducted on real quantum hardware validate the cost-effective performance of the proposed method.

title: Scheduling for Hybrid Microgrids with Renewable Energy Sources and Hydrogen Storage: Data-Correlated Uncertainty Modeling and Semi-Convex Relaxation
abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources (RESs), hydrogen energy storage (HES), and electric vehicles (EVs) is critical to the decarbonization of electric power production; however, it introduces significant challenges for microgrid energy management owing principally to RES uncertainty and the non-convex constraints associated with HES and EV operations. The present work addresses these challenges by applying data-driven uncertainty set optimization and semi-convex relaxation approaches. First, a probability-driven data-correlated uncertainty set is developed using historical data distributions to generate RES uncertainty representations with reduced conservativeness under significantly reduced computational burden. Second, a closed-loop semi-convex relaxation procedure is designed to manage the non-convex operational constraints of HES and EV operations, where the NP-hard nature of these constraints is addressed by iteratively enforcing only violated binary conditions, which ensures solution accuracy with minimal computational overhead. Third, the resulting tri-level robust energy management model is solved efficiently by a customized column-and-constraint generation algorithm incorporating the proposed relaxation procedure. As a result, only those non-convex constraints that are violated in the relaxed solution are included in the energy management solution process. The superiority of the proposed approach over existing state-of-the-art methods in enabling higher penetrations of clean energy technologies is demonstrated through numerical case studies on a practical hybrid microgrid system.

title: Rotor-Angle Stability Enhancement Control for MMC-MTDC Systems Without Sending-End Power Reserves
abstract: High-voltage direct current (HVDC) systems are increasingly integrated into AC grids, making rotor-angle stability more critical. Improper HVDC dynamics during disturbances may weaken synchronizing torque and damping, thereby aggravating oscillations. This paper investigates the offshore wind farm (OWF)-based multi-terminal DC (MTDC) system and analyzes the impact of its power injections on grid rotor-angle stability. On this basis, a frequency-based power control logic is first proposed to enhance rotor-angle stability. Building on this logic, Lyapunov-based control laws are derived to coordinate active and reactive power both among multiple terminals (inter-terminal level) and within each converter under capacity constraints (intra-terminal level). To further optimize the coordinated control, an optimization framework is then designed, ensuring effective and secure support. Finally, considering the absence of power reserves at the sending-end OWF, a capacitor energy-based control strategy is proposed for MTDC systems to utilize all MMCs' capacitor energy at the same time for stability support (device level), thereby expanding the available support energy and further improving rotor-angle stability. The effectiveness and robustness of the proposed control are validated on the IEEE 39-bus system via PSCAD/EMTDC and MATLAB co-simulation.

title: Multi-Source Coordinated Frequency Control of Grid-Connected Wind-Solar-Storage Power Station With Economic Improvement
abstract: Renewable power plant participating in frequency regulation often compromises power generation efficiency, and existing frequency regulation strategies generally neglect economic cost. To improve frequency security and economic efficiency, the paper proposes a multi-source coordinated frequency control (MCFC) for wind-solar-storage hybrid power stations. The MCFC control consists of two stages: frequency support and frequency recovery. During frequency support, photovoltaic (PV), wind, and energy storage are sequentially activated according to dynamic characteristics. The strategy allocates wind, PV, and energy storage outputs based on frequency security constraints to avoid excessive use of regulation energy and improve economic efficiency. During frequency recovery, wind turbine rotor speed is smoothly restored, and the recovery of the energy storage system (ESS) state of charge (SOC) is explicitly considered. Case studies are undertaken on the two-area power system with a wind-solar-storage hybrid power station and Guangshui hybrid collection station. The results show that MCFC can restore the frequency above safety thresholds and minimize renewable regulation energy to improve economic efficiency. Compared with existing methods, MCFC not only restores frequency to 49.5 Hz under a wider range of disturbances but also reduces economic index by up to 40% under mild disturbances.

title: Negative-Sequence Impedance Provision of A Virtual Admittance-Based Inverter-Based Resource
abstract: While some grid-forming (GFM) inverter-based resources (IBRs) have both positive- and negative-sequence control units equipped to provide desired negative-sequence impedance, we find that a virtual admittance-based GFM-IBR with only positive-sequence unit can also provide desired negative-sequence impedance for grid code compliance. The goal of this paper is to provide an analysis to relate the negative-sequence impedance provision with the control scheme. To this end, an electromagnetic transient (EMT) testbed is developed to examine an IBR's behavior subject to unbalanced grid faults. The negative-sequence voltage and current components are measured to calculate the equivalent negative-sequence impedance empirically. It is found that this impedance is indeed associated with the virtual impedance. The underlying mechanism is further discovered through complex vector-based analysis and frame conversion. The major takeaways are two-fold: (i) For a given control scheme, its negative-sequence impedance can be found analytically; (ii) inverter control can be designed more concisely to provide both positive- and negative-sequence impedances, in contract of having more complicated design with both positive- and negative-sequence control units included.

title: Anticipatory Utility Operations with Long-Duration Hydrogen Storage and Carbon Market Synergies
abstract: When leveraged within carbon market mechanisms, hydrogen energy storage systems (HESS) offer a viable option for supporting low-carbon operation in vertically integrated utilities. However, a key challenge is that short-term operational decisions are made without explicit visibility of their long-term consequences, which are reflected through cumulative hydro gen and carbon constraints that ensure system feasibility. To bridge this time-scale gap, this paper proposes a reinforcement learning–augmented primal–dual rolling-horizon optimization framework. A trained future-aware regularizer incorporates long-term information into short-term decision-making, while a primal–dual scheme enforces cumulative constraints on hydrogen and carbon markets with computational tractability. Numerical studies on the IEEE 6-bus, 118-bus, and 300-bus test systems demonstrate the framework's effectiveness and scalability. Results demonstrate that the proposed framework keeps annual terminal residuals negligible while reducing peak emissions, improving economic performance, and enabling seasonal load shifting across different system scales.

title: Risk Assessment of Forced SSO Excited by DFIG-Originated Interharmonics
abstract: The forced subsynchronous oscillations (FSSOs) induced by the doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG)-originated interharmonics can degrade power quality and threaten the security of equipment as well as the power system. This study investigates the generation mechanisms of DFIG-originated interharmonics, and proposes a novel criterion of the impedance-based method that reveals the excitation mechanisms of FSSOs. Subsequently, a severity index for FSSOs, defined as the interharmonic amplitude ratio (IAR), is established to quantify the FSSO severity. A methodology is developed to compute the probability distribution of this severity function, incorporating the probabilistic characteristics of system operating conditions and wind speeds. Building upon this severity index and its probability distribution, a risk matrix integrating two distinct risk dimensions, power quality degradation risk and equipment/system security risks, is constructed to assess FSSO risk. The proposed methodology is validated through comprehensive time-domain simulations. Simulation results demonstrate that both risk types are highly sensitive to the probabilistic characteristics of grid operating conditions and wind speed profiles. Specifically, when the grid operates with high probability under weak-grid conditions, and the DFIG rotor frequency corresponding to average wind speed falls within 5/6∼7/6 times the fundamental frequency, the system experiences elevated levels of both FSSO-induced risks.

title: Dynamic Interaction Modeling and Stability Analysis for Grid-Connected Renewable Energy Systems with High Inertia Energy Storage Synchronous Condenser
abstract: The high inertia energy storage synchronous condenser (HIESSC), which integrates the doubly-fed machine technology with flywheel energy storage, has recently emerged as a promising means to support both frequency and voltage regulation in renewable energy sources (RESs). Despite its novelty, the impact of the HIESSC on system oscillations and the interactions among the control loops of RES stations remains unclear. This paper examines a grid-connected system comprising the HIESSC and a grid-connected converter with grid-following control (GCC-GFL). Firstly, a single-input-single-output interaction model is developed through equivalent block diagram transformations. By incorporating the grid-side coupling impedance and transfer functions of interacting subsystems, the proposed model reveals how the HIESSC modifies the dynamic characteristics of GCC-GFL through a feedback control perspective. Subsequently, the impact of HIESSC operating modes and operating points on the small-signal stability is analyzed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed methods and analyses is validated by the experiments.

title: Available-Power-Constrained Coordinated Fault Voltage Support Control for Multiple Inverter-Interfaced DGs
abstract: The increasing prevalence of weak grid conditions necessitates that inverter-interfaced distributed generators (IIDGs) support voltage during faults to prevent further disturbances. However, maximizing IIDGs' voltage support capability while respecting operational constraints to prevent unintended tripping remains challenging. This paper proposes an available-power-constrained coordinated fault voltage support control strategy for multiple IIDGs. First, based on the fault characteristics of resistive-inductive distribution networks (DN), a current reference strategy is developed to maximize each IIDG's voltage support contribution. Then, considering constraints of non-fault-phase voltage and power fluctuation, the safe operating domain of each IIDG is derived. On this basis, an adaptive fault voltage support control framework is constructed, where a zonal clustering method enables communication free coordinated control among multiple IIDGs. In addition, the applicable condition of the proposed method is quantified using the grid short-circuit ratio (SCR) of the grid. Simulation results show that, for case of SCR lower than 3, the proposed method can improve the fault voltage of DNs by 30.8%.

title: Stability Analysis and Parametric Feasible-Region Characterization of Multi-Oscillation Modes in GFL-GFM Hybrid Systems Under Wide Scale Grid Strength
abstract: This paper investigates the stability of multi-low-frequency oscillation (LFO) modes in grid-connected hybrid systems with grid-following (GFL) and grid-forming (GFM) converters. The objective is to reveal the coupling oscillation mechanism between dual-source power and control parameters under wide variations in grid strength, and to construct a stable operating domain. A reduced-order model balancing accuracy and complexity is established, and a decoupled equivalent damping analysis method is proposed to quantitatively characterize the stability of the dominant GFL and GFM oscillation modes from the perspective of damping formation mechanism. It is found that the GFL-dominated and GFM-dominated oscillation modes exhibit opposite stability evolution trends with respect to grid strength and are constrained by the dual-source power coupling effect. As a result, a single fixed parameter set cannot ensure stable system operation across a wide range of grid strengths and full power operating conditions. Furthermore, the influence of key control parameters on the oscillation modes is clarified, and stable parameter boundaries under extreme operating conditions are determined. Time-domain simulations validate the accuracy of the theoretical analysis and the proposed stable domain construction method.

title: Bilevel Optimization for Green Hydrogen-to-Ammonia Synthesis System Considering Complex Dynamic Processes and Uncertainties
abstract: The wind-powered green hydrogen-to-ammonia system offers a promising pathway for utilizing marine renewable energy; however, its economic viability is constrained by the strongly nonlinear dynamics of ammonia synthesis and the inherent stochasticity of wind power generation. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a bilevel scheduling framework. In the upper layer, a reduced-order Trend- and Structure-constrained Physics-Informed Neural Network (TS-PINN) model is developed by embedding trend priors and mechanistic constraints, effectively capturing the nonlinear characteristics of the ammonia synthesis process with significantly reduced computational effort. An improved Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) algorithm is then employed to co‑optimize operational strategies and key reactor setpoints, including bed temperature and pressure. In the lower layer, a Wasserstein‑distance‑based distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model is established to coordinate hydrogen production and storage operations to hedge against wind power uncertainty. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an effective balance among modeling accuracy, economic performance, and operational robustness, while accounting for coupled reaction–heat‑transfer dynamics and renewable generation uncertainty.

title: Distributed Adaptive Coordination of Flexibility Resources for Real-Time Power Balancing in Islanded DC Microgrids
abstract: Modern DC microgrids (DC-MGs) typically incorporate Renewable Energy Sources (RESs), energy storage systems, and local loads. In islanded DC-MGs, effective coordination of these components is essential for secure and reliable operation, given the intermittent nature of RESs and the uncertain demand profile. This paper employs electric spring topology to enhance flexibility through the smart management of both energy stored in batteries, and loads, in the case that the generation capacity of multiple RESs-operating with the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm-is insufficient to meet demand. Besides, a distributed adaptive droop-based scheme is designed concerning a trade-off between common bus voltage regulation and proper current/power sharing among units. This distributed scheme benefits from a low-bandwidth communication interface among the in-service units to collect required data for adaptive estimation of droop gains. To ensure reliable operation of the DCMG, batteries' capacity and State-of-Charge (SoC) information are also incorporated into the energy-sharing strategy, aiming to maintain SoC balance among storage units during replenishment. The feasibility of the proposed approach is evaluated through a Power-Hardware-in-the-Loop (PHIL) platform.

title: Event-Driven Restoration of Interconnected Distribution Systems with R-SOPs Adapting to Continuous Disasters and Uncertainties
abstract: Extreme disasters lead to continuous and large scale faults in distribution systems (DSs), posing challenges in developing practical restoration strategies. This paper proposes a pre-disaster prevention and post-disaster restoration framework for R-SOP-enabled interconnected distribution systems (IDSs), which accounts for the persistence of fault evolution and the uncertainties of renewable energy and load. Unlike most existing studies that focus on individual DSs and fixed fault scenarios, this paper employs a reconfigurable soft open point (R-SOP) with asymmetric converter design. Through its feeder selection and converter reconfiguration mechanisms, the R-SOP enables efficient capacity utilization and dynamic interconnection between multiple DSs, and additionally addresses, in a unified manner, the dual uncertainty of stochastic fluctuations and sudden faults under continuous disasters. In the pre-disaster phase, electric buses (EBs) are deployed based on restoration simulations to reduce potential load shedding and shorten travel distances post disaster. In the post-disaster phase, an event-driven restoration is developed, where predefined fault events and error events dynamically update restoration strategies to adapt to continuous faults and uncertainties. By combining R-SOP-assisted recon figuration with coordinated scheduling of flexible resources, the proposed method overcomes the limitations of individual-network restoration, enhancing system resilience. Simulation results based on a modified 102-node IDS show that the proposed method not only accelerates service restoration under continuous extreme events but also ensures voltage security.

title: Graph Neural Network with Dual-Stream Attention for Global Maximum Power Point Tracking under Partial Shading Conditions
abstract: Due to the complex nonlinear coupling between circuit topology and environmental changes, precise maximum power point tracking under partial shading conditions remains a challenge. Existing data-driven methods typically view photovoltaic (PV) arrays as unstructured feature vectors or Euclidean grids, which fail to capture the fundamental series parallel constraints that control the distribution of current and voltage. This study proposes a graph neural network with dual stream attention (GNN-DSA), which is a physical perception framework that can strictly decouple static topologies from dynamic environmental signals. Static streams encode arrays into message-passed directed graphs with specific edge types that capture series-parallel circuit constraints, while dynamic streams capture irradiation patterns through the Transformer. A novel bidirectional cross-attention mechanism explicitly simulates the interaction between circuit constraints and environmental stress. Hardware verification indicates that the tracking efficiency of GNN-DSA on real PV panels is 99.1%–99.6%, on solar array simulators is 99.99%, and the response time is less than 100ms. Comparative analysis shows that compared with the multilayer perceptron baseline, GNN-DSA reduces the mean squared error by 45.6%, and compared with the state-of-the-art Crossformer model, it reduces it by 22.3%.

title: Hybrid Fault Isolation and Power Control of Wind Turbine Generators based on Stacked UIO
abstract: The stable operation of megawatt-class wind turbines directly impacts grid connection performance. As complex electromechanical systems operating in variable environments, time-varying hybrid faults frequently occur, posing challenges for fault-tolerant control (FTC). This paper proposes novel approaches for hybrid fault diagnosis and fault-tolerant controller design. First, a collaborative architecture for a stacked unknown input observer (UIO) is constructed for integrated fault diagnosis of hybrid faults in wind turbine generators (WTGs). The designed stacked UIO strategy can decouple and separately estimate the dynamic of speed and torque, achieving effective time-varying hybrid fault diagnosis. Second, given the disturbances, uncertainties, and discrete-time nature of WTGs, the asymptotic stability of the proposed UIO is established using Lyapunov's theorem. Finally, combining fault information, a two-degree-of-freedom model predictive control strategy is adopted to achieve FTC while also considering power stability tracking. Simulation results show that the proposed method can estimate time-varying faults in WTG actuators and sensors, and maintain reliable control performance under hybrid fault conditions, thereby verifying its effectiveness as a comprehensive FTC solution.

title: AnAdaptive Graph Convolution-based Bi-level Planning Strategy for Urban Fast-Charging Stations in Electricity-Transportation Coupled Networks
abstract: To address the mismatch between massive charging requirement triggers and limited charging resource supply in Electricity-Transportation Coupled Networks (ETCNs), this paper proposes a bi-level planning strategy for urban fast-charging stations (FCSs). First, given the topological interdependence and feature interactions of ETCNs, a unified graph-structured representation model is constructed to characterize the dynamic transmission of energy and information among multiple agents in “vehicles-stations-networks”. Second, adaptive graph convolution is designed in the upper layer. Through multi-order neighborhood aggregation and adaptive weights, the inherent physical-electrical correlation knowledge among multiple agents is learned, enabling multi-dimensional feature extraction of ETCNs and differentiated weight allocation to transportation nodes. The physical constraints of ETCN operation are embedded in the feature loss as regularization, thereby constructing a semi-supervised learning paradigm driven by data-feature collaboration loss. Then, based on the candidate FCS set initially screened by the upper layer, an equilibrium evaluation index is established to suppress node congestion and service blind areas. In the lower layer, a multi-objective optimization model is constructed to jointly solve the connection location of FCSs in the electricity network and the capacity configuration of charging piles. Finally, case studies are conducted within a practical functional zone in Hong Kong, China. Experimental results verify the superiority of the proposed method under different planning scenarios.
